name: KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION
subject: Transparency should always come first...
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
We need leaders who put transparency first.

| | | | | |
---
| |

Dear Peter,Leadership is not just about decisions.
It is about **how those decisions are made**.And in Johnson County, that matters now more than ever.When Mike Kelly became Commission Chair, one of his early decisions was to **remove public comments from the live stream**.Think about that.At a time when residents rely on access and transparency, the ability to hear directly from the public was taken away from those who could not attend in person. That decision has since been reversed. But it speaks to a broader pattern.Because this is not just about one decision. It is about a leadership style that too often operates behind the scenes and within a small circle. We have seen **work groups formed with limited commissioner participation** , including a housing work group with only three commissioners represented.When decisions are shaped in smaller, closed settings, it raises a simple question:**Who is at the table and who is not?** And more importantly:**Where is the voice of the taxpayer in those conversations?**
---
|
---
| |

Transparency is not selective.
It is not convenient.
And it is not something you turn on and off.It is a commitment to openness and accountability.I am running for Johnson County Commission Chair because I believe leadership should be different.It should be open to all commissioners.
Accessible to the public.
And accountable for every decision that impacts your tax dollars and your community.But changing that culture will not happen without a real effort.
---
| [DONATE TODAY](https://us.list-manage.com/yYr0qj8MAcB?e=7320325a61&c2id=7adf4106091b2bdf32986c5b36d3a494)
---
| |
Your support helps us reach voters, share what is really happening, and build a campaign strong enough to restore transparency and accountability in Johnson County.If you believe leadership should include people, not exclude them, I am asking you to stand with me. Together, we can bring openness and trust back to county government.With determination,
**Karen Crnkovich
** Candidate for Johnson County Commission Chair

body:
Hi there, it’s Nancy Lacore, the Democrat running to flip South Carolina’s First District.
I have a lot of thoughts about what’s been going on with Pete Hegseth.
Not only did he remove me from my position as Chief of the Navy Reserve after 35 years of service, but he’s actively undermining the foundation of our military.
Hegseth has fired more than a dozen senior military officers, including an Army chief of staff and two other generals who were ousted recently.
And now, he’s waging a war with Iran that could put our national security and countless American lives on the line.
That kind of behavior isn’t just destabilizing – it’s dangerous.
Now more than ever, we need leadership that’s rooted in honor, service, and respect. And that’s exactly why I’m running for Congress in South Carolina’s First District.
If we’re going to flip this seat and take back a Democratic House Majority, I need your help. Can you make a split donation of $25 or whatever you can, to Resist Reclaim Rebuild and my campaign? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]
DONATE NOW TO HELP NANCY FLIP THIS SEAT! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]
I’ll be honest, folks, I’m concerned.
While global tensions rise, the last thing we need is reckless leadership that’s willing to gamble with American lives.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others. In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime. Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? Tell Congress:
Tax Big Oil Profits, Return Money to Everyday People!

Big Oil is using the war with Iran to profit off of everyday people who are
already struggling to make ends meet. Gas prices are out of control — up more
than 30% on average since the start of Trump’s current term. The American people need relief, and it should come from Big Oil’s profits.

Under the Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act, any extra profits billionaire oil
executives make by over-charging their customers would be returned to the public
instead of lining their already-deep pockets even further.

Tell Congress: tax Big Oil profits and return the funds to everyday people! https://links.messages.lcv. ADD YOUR NAME https://links.messages.lcv. Peter, Gas prices are soaring. Americans are broke. Gas companies are raking in record
profits. Trump's war in Iran is making everything worse. Here's how we fix it: To stop Big Oil and Gas from taking advantage of customers, Sen. Sheldon
Whitehouse (RI) and Rep. Ro Khanna (CA-17) introduced the Big Oil Windfall
Profits Tax Act. Under this bill, large oil companies would pay a tax on each
barrel of oil they produce or import above the average price in 2025. Revenue
from the tax would be returned to customers, who would receive about $216 to
$324 in rebates per year. Join LCV in calling on Congress to pass The Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act! https://links.messages.lcv. For more than a year, we’ve all been feeling the pain of Trump’s broken
promises. Energy costs were already unaffordable before the war began, and now working families’ wallets are taking
an even greater hit: The average price of a gallon of gas in the U.S. has increased by over 50% since Trump’s war in Iran began — jumping from $2.98 to $4.51. In 2025, Trump’s insistence on dirty oil, gas, and coal drove up electric bills by 13%. Now, with prices rising daily, Trump continues to block clean, affordable energy — like wind and solar — here at home. It’s time to usher in a new era of accountability for Trump and Big Oil’s
corporate greed. Take action today and urge Congress to pass the Big Oil Windfall Profits Tax Act. https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/3Z0ec-8_ As long as the U.S. remains dependent on fossil fuels, working families will
keep paying the price — not only shrinking our wallets, but also our health,
safety, and future. The solution is building clean energy close to home,
creating power sources that lower costs, create jobs, and that are sustainable
for our communities and our climate. Thank you for taking action with LCV — for people and for our planet. Leah Donahey

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Committee to Elect Justin J
body:

---
Peter, I'm emailing you more motivated than ever before.

**Republicans passed their racist, outrageous gerrymandered districts in Tennessee that eliminate District 9 as the only majority-Black and majority-Democratic district in our state.**

They have cheated their way into a map that favors Republicans, where politicians are picking their voters instead of voters picking their leaders.

We need to call this what it is: **this new map is a political lynching** — an affront to justice and the fight for equality.

My heart aches for my hometown of Memphis, where I was born and raised and where generations of my family are buried. [](https://jj-p.org/l/uCrwin9kMGmD) **But I refuse to give in to despair. Don't give up hope, Peter.** The fight still carries on, renewed with urgency as we work to restore the rights that our ancestors marched, prayed, bled, and died for.

[This righteous fight for our rights has never been more important, to push back against Jim Crow 2.0, to end the corruption that runs rampant and free, to give Black and Brown People a true voice in their democracy. Our fight continues: Will you please join me against authoritarianism and chip in $5 right away?](https://jj-p.org/l/YcUF9sjxfRil) | [CONTRIBUTE $5 »](https://jj-p.org/l/q7uMUMACdIFT)
---
The Supreme Court's ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_ cleared the path for this, and I'm sure we're going to see the same playbook in other states soon, robbing Black and Brown People of their voting rights.

Last week, Republicans stole the only Black-majority district from us. But I want you to know: No matter what they do, no matter how much they try to break us and make us bend and quit — **we will still be here.**

I'm still going to fight to demonstrate strong leadership in TN, and I hope that you, as a member of this People-powered Movement, are still by my side.

This isn't over, and we will not stop until justice rolls down like waters and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream. [Will you chip in $5 or more in the next 30 minutes to fight this authoritarian power grab?](https://jj-p.org/l/hHCwnYvJCzPh)

Mother's Day marked the beginning of **National Women 's Health Week (May 10-16, 2026)** -- a national initiative led by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to encourage women to prioritize their physical, mental, and long-term health.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..vucwHe97Ak9_xeTpInIv7zc6QQFjt52OIs0RrPGfru8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=197601907)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/86009455-ec14-46df-b787-cc885bbeac30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---

[National Women's Health Week](https://substack.com/redirect/87968324-9c65-443a-b7c4-c0c1d0f80ac9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This year's theme is:
**" Prevention, Innovation, and Impact: A New Era in Women's Health."**
[2026 National Women's Health Week Theme](https://substack.com/redirect/8ad06676-42c2-4c60-a43d-f735f8f1b4e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It is an important message -- and one that extends far beyond healthcare alone.
In medicine, the best outcomes often come from early awareness, early detection, and early intervention. Preventive care reduces suffering, lowers long-term costs, improves quality of life, and strengthens families and communities.
_**That same mindset has value across nearly every area of public policy.**_
Too often, institutions and governments are _**reactive rather than proactive**_. Problems are addressed only after they become expensive, disruptive, or politically unavoidable. Whether the issue is healthcare access, chronic disease, mental health, infrastructure, affordability, education, or economic stability, the cost of waiting is usually far greater than the cost of prevention.
_**National Women 's Health Week serves as a reminder that prevention is not simply a medical concept -- it is a governing principle.**_
According to the Office on Women's Health, this year's initiative emphasizes:
* preventive screenings and early detection,
* chronic disease prevention,
* women-specific health research,
* innovation in care delivery,
* mental health,
* healthy aging,
* and improving long-term health outcomes for women across every stage of life.
[National Women's Health Week Focus Areas](https://substack.com/redirect/15130399-1c84-4cf8-8122-b1cc7d8c4b2e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

_**These priorities matter because women often serve as the backbone of families, caregivers for multiple generations, leaders in their communities, and a critical part of the healthcare workforce itself.**_
At the same time, America faces growing healthcare pressures:
* rising costs,
* physician and nursing shortages,
* burnout among healthcare workers,
* increased chronic disease,
* mental health challenges,
* and growing frustration with systems that often feel administrative rather than patient-centered.

**The conversation around prevention is also backed by substantial economic data.**
According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, chronic diseases account for the vast majority of healthcare spending in the United States, with many conditions heavily influenced by preventable risk factors and delayed intervention.
[CDC Chronic Disease Overview](https://substack.com/redirect/026f8869-339f-4bfc-8f5e-76602ee0a970?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services estimates that U.S. healthcare spending continues to consume a significant share of the national economy and is increasing.
[CMS National Health Expenditure Data](https://substack.com/redirect/42504507-1ec9-4923-85bf-b859714818ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Prevention is not only compassionate policy. It is economically responsible policy.
And while National Women's Health Week focuses specifically on women's health, the broader lesson applies nationally: societies function better when they anticipate challenges rather than simply react to crises.
That includes:
* investing in preventive healthcare,
* strengthening maternal and mental health resources,
* supporting medical research,
* addressing workforce burnout,
* modernizing infrastructure before failures occur,
* improving environmental resilience,
* and focusing on long-term outcomes rather than short-term political cycles.

A healthier society requires long-term thinking.
_**This week is an opportunity to recognize the women who hold families and communities together while also embracing a broader national mindset rooted in prevention, innovation, preparation, and practical solutions.**_
_**Let 's continue honoring the women of America throughout National Women's Health Week -- and carry the spirit of prevention, innovation, and impact into every level of leadership and public policy.**_

clean_body: Prevention, Innovation, and Impact Should Guide More Than Healthcare | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found Prevention, Innovation, and Impact Should Guide More Than Healthcare | | | May 15 | | | | | | | | | | | | Mother's Day marked the beginning of National Women 's Health Week (May 10-16, 2026) -- a national initiative led by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to encourage women to prioritize their physical, mental, and long-term health. | | ---|---|--- This year's theme is: " Prevention, Innovation, and Impact: A New Era in Women's Health." It is an important message -- and one that extends far beyond healthcare alone. In medicine, the best outcomes often come from early awareness, early detection, and early intervention. Preventive care reduces suffering, lowers long-term costs, improves quality of life, and strengthens families and communities. That same mindset has value across nearly every area of public policy. Too often, institutions and governments are reactive rather than proactive. Problems are addressed only after they become expensive, disruptive, or politically unavoidable. Whether the issue is healthcare access, chronic disease, mental health, infrastructure, affordability, education, or economic stability, the cost of waiting is usually far greater than the cost of prevention. National Women 's Health Week serves as a reminder that prevention is not simply a medical concept -- it is a governing principle. According to the Office on Women's Health, this year's initiative emphasizes: preventive screenings and early detection, chronic disease prevention, women-specific health research, innovation in care delivery, mental health, healthy aging, and improving long-term health outcomes for women across every stage of life. These priorities matter because women often serve as the backbone of families, caregivers for multiple generations, leaders in their communities, and a critical part of the healthcare workforce itself. At the same time, America faces growing healthcare pressures: rising costs, physician and nursing shortages, burnout among healthcare workers, increased chronic disease, mental health challenges, and growing frustration with systems that often feel administrative rather than patient-centered. The conversation around prevention is also backed by substantial economic data. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, chronic diseases account for the vast majority of healthcare spending in the United States, with many conditions heavily influenced by preventable risk factors and delayed intervention. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services estimates that U.S. healthcare spending continues to consume a significant share of the national economy and is increasing. Prevention is not only compassionate policy. It is economically responsible policy. And while National Women's Health Week focuses specifically on women's health, the broader lesson applies nationally: societies function better when they anticipate challenges rather than simply react to crises. That includes: investing in preventive healthcare, strengthening maternal and mental health resources, supporting medical research, addressing workforce burnout, modernizing infrastructure before failures occur, improving environmental resilience, and focusing on long-term outcomes rather than short-term political cycles. A healthier society requires long-term thinking. This week is an opportunity to recognize the women who hold families and communities together while also embracing a broader national mindset rooted in prevention, innovation, preparation, and practical solutions. Let 's continue honoring the women of America throughout National Women's Health Week -- and carry the spirit of prevention, innovation, and impact into every level of leadership and public policy.** The Goldstein Substack is free today. | | | Hi Peter, People in Colorado's jails who aren’t serving time for felony convictions, those who haven't been convicted of anything, or are serving time for misdemeanors, still have the right to vote. For years, very few of them did. The year I started asking questions,**just three (out of several hundred) eligible voters actually voted** from the Jefferson County jail**.** I asked to bring in-person voting into my county's jail. **They told me no.** **So** **I helped pass a law requiring it.** Turnout in my county's jail went from **less than 1% to over 40% in a single election.** One of the first people to vote from jail after the law changed told me it was one of the top experiences of his life. **He said it made him feel like he mattered.** That's why I do this work. And that's why I'm running for Secretary of State—to make sure your voice is heard and your vote is counted. We’re in the homestretch and I’m making every dollar count. **" Corpus Christi moves toward mandatory 25% cut in water use if emergency is declared"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/89da882e-3e25-4bba-8502-bc21fe846b24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Alex Nguyen** and **Colleen DeGuzman** - Corpus Christi residents and businesses -- including one of the nation's largest petrochemical corridors -- may be required to cut water use by 25% during a water emergency that city leaders expect to hit by September unless a devastating drought eases.

The City Council voted 7-2 Tuesday to give initial approval to a water curtailment plan that would set water limits for different customers, ranging from residents and local businesses to large oil companies. The council is expected to take a final vote adopting the curtailment plan on May 19.

City leaders for months have been bracing for a Level 1 water emergency -- the point when the city's supply is projected to be 180 days away from falling short of demand. If there's no significant rainfall soon, experts are predicting that may be around four months away. _([TX TRIB](https://substack.com/redirect/89da882e-3e25-4bba-8502-bc21fe846b24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Report: Texas public schools have largest non-Covid enrollment drop in recorded history"** via [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/30f9ba0a-1dad-4d8b-a3d4-df554846c131?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Adam Schwager** - Total public school enrollment in Texas dropped by over 76,000 students, according to a Texas 2036 report released on Monday morning. The 2025-26 school year is only the second time public school education has dropped in recorded Texas history, dating back to the 1987-88 school year. The other recorded drop happened in the 2020-21 school year, during the height of the COVID-19 shutdowns.

The enrollment drop is happening across the state, with only the Abilene area seeing an increase in enrollment, and only certain areas in central and east Texas holding steady. The biggest drops are taking place in south and west Texas, with the Midland, Amarillo, Edinburg, and San Angelo regions all losing at least 2.5% of their student population.

"(The decline is) spread out across all types of students, it's spread out across all areas of the state," **Mary Lynn Pruneda** , the Director of Education and Workforce Policy for Texas 2036, said. "So that makes it really hard to point to one particular thing and say, 'Yes, this is definitely the reason that there are fewer kids in public schools today.'

Schools are also disproportionately losing Hispanic and White students. While the overall public school population dropped 1.4%, the Hispanic population dropped by 2.1% and the White population dropped by 1.9%. Overall, Hispanic students made up 81% of the loss enrollment loss. The data also shows declines in traditionally underserved communities -- with homeless students dropping by 8% and economically disadvantaged students dropping by 2.3%. _([KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/30f9ba0a-1dad-4d8b-a3d4-df554846c131?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" CBP axes plan to build portion of border wall in Big Bend National Park"** via [Spectrum News](https://substack.com/redirect/f26bd839-73d6-4e31-8be3-fe83ee32c8a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) -- A top U.S. Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) official told the Washington Examiner that plans to build a 30-foot-tall border wall in Big Bend National Park have been axed.

CBP Commissioner **Rodney Scott** told the Examiner it would be "kind of silly" to put a border wall on top of the park's towering granite cliffs.

Instead of the physical barrier, Scott said officials will pave roads along the border of the national park and utilize drones and other digital surveillance equipment.

"So what we're trying to convey is that we are going to have meaningful border security in that entire area," Scott said. _([Spectrum News](https://substack.com/redirect/f26bd839-73d6-4e31-8be3-fe83ee32c8a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" Excessive heat suspected as cause of death after six bodies found in rail car near Laredo"** via [The Texas Tribune](https://substack.com/redirect/d32d4294-ad95-4819-9137-bb2a042defaf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s**Berenice Garcia** and **Alex Nguyen** - Extreme heat is suspected to have played a role in the deaths of six people from Mexico and Honduras whose bodies were discovered inside a train car in Laredo.

A 29-year-old woman from Mexico and a 24-year-old man from Honduras were among the six deceased individuals found inside a shipping container at Union Pacific Railyard on Sunday afternoon, according to Webb County officials. The other four individuals were all male and included one teenager, though their identities had not yet been confirmed.

The Webb County Medical Examiner determined that the woman died due to hyperthermia, or overheating. Hyperthermia is also suspected to have caused the death of the other five individuals, though formal examinations for them are still pending, according to a news release issued by the county.

**Corinne Stern** , the county's medical examiner, found identification cards and cellphones that indicated the individuals were from Mexico and Honduras, according to the Associated Press. **" Report reveals how much water could be consumed by Texas data centers"** via [Houston Chronicle](https://substack.com/redirect/0873c39b-91d2-49e1-abb1-3c0383b02bbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Michael Garcia** - Texas' booming data center industry could strain the state's already stressed water supply, with facilities projected to account for up to 9% of statewide water use by 2040, according to a University of Texas study.

**" Gas power leapfrogs wind for first time in 10 years in Texas' grid connection queue"** via [San Antonio Report](https://substack.com/redirect/e96abab3-608d-4a8b-9a0b-ff3969c3b89d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Brandon Mulder** - A decade ago, wind power was surging in popularity and attracting huge investments that made Texas a national leader in renewable energy. But today, gas generation is making a big comeback, driven by a wave of data centers flooding into the state.

For the last six months, the volume of gas generation in the Texas grid's interconnection queue -- the yearslong waiting list for electric generators wanting to connect to the grid -- has surpassed wind. It's the first time since January 2016 that gas has overtaken wind in the queue, a shift that reflects the policy and economic headwinds facing the wind industry and data centers favoring gas power as they seek to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom.

"The data center explosion and their desire for 24/7 power probably excited a lot of gas developers, and that gas queue got bigger," said University of Texas professor of energy regulation **David Spence**.

Like every power grid operator in the U.S., the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, or ERCOT, uses the interconnection queue to manage and plan for new power generation coming online. But not all projects in the queue ultimately reach completion. According to the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, or LBNL, only 22% of projects in ERCOT's queue actually get built, which is still the highest percentage of any grid in the nation. _([SA REPORT](https://substack.com/redirect/e96abab3-608d-4a8b-9a0b-ff3969c3b89d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

**" 300+ cases filed so far in new Texas business court and experts say more are coming"** via [KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/4ce6240b-ce9b-4a92-9a0b-1485124391ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'s **Dylan McKim** \-- State leaders were quick to take credit after Dell Technologies announced last week it plans to reincorporate its business in the Lone Star State where it is already headquartered. State Rep. **Jeff Leach** , R - Plano, posted on his X account following the Dell announcement, 'It's a direct result of the work we've been doing to strengthen our business climate'. Gov. **Greg Abbott** celebrated the news on his X account saying 'more businesses are sure to follow'; The move by Dell will not affect any operations or move any new employees to Texas but the move signals a result of the changes made to the state's corporate laws.

For years, Texas lagged behind other states like Delaware that had more business-friendly laws and sophisticated business courts that attracted millions of companies to incorporate within its borders. Incorporating in a state -- or making it your legal home -- means the company's internal affairs are governed by that state's specific laws. It is not uncommon for companies to operate in one state but be incorporated in another.

In the past two legislative sessions in Austin, lawmakers were able to finally create and expand the Texas Business Court and lowered corporate accountability. The courts started hearing cases in September 2024. Between 2024 and 2025 the state saw a 12% increase in the number of out-of-state limited liability companies that filed to do business in Texas, according to data from the Texas Secretary of State's (SOS) office. It's hard to determine if that increase is due to changes at the legislative level, but a spokesperson for the SOS said the increase was consistent with long-term growth in the state.

The Texas Business Court consists of 11 divisions of judges that have specific expertise in complex business cases. The judges are appointed by the governor and serve two-year terms. Currently only five divisions are operating and they all encompass Texas's urban areas. **Brad Foster** , a partner at Haynes Boone, said creating a specialized court in Texas for business disputes was necessary. In the past, Texas-based companies would sometimes have to leave the state for disputes if they were not incorporated here. "You could have a dispute between two Dallas or Houston based people and they would be having to go to Delaware, hire Delaware lawyers and litigate their dispute -- that really is only a Texas dispute -- up there," Foster explained. _([KXAN](https://substack.com/redirect/4ce6240b-ce9b-4a92-9a0b-1485124391ba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg))_

TOP NEWS " Corpus Christi moves toward mandatory 25% cut in water use if emergency is declared" via Alex Nguyen and Colleen DeGuzman - Corpus Christi residents and businesses -- including one of the nation's largest petrochemical corridors -- may be required to cut water use by 25% during a water emergency that city leaders expect to hit by September unless a devastating drought eases. The City Council voted 7-2 Tuesday to give initial approval to a water curtailment plan that would set water limits for different customers, ranging from residents and local businesses to large oil companies. The council is expected to take a final vote adopting the curtailment plan on May 19. City leaders for months have been bracing for a Level 1 water emergency -- the point when the city's supply is projected to be 180 days away from falling short of demand. If there's no significant rainfall soon, experts are predicting that may be around four months away. () " Report: Texas public schools have largest non-Covid enrollment drop in recorded history" via Adam Schwager - Total public school enrollment in Texas dropped by over 76,000 students, according to a Texas 2036 report released on Monday morning. The 2025-26 school year is only the second time public school education has dropped in recorded Texas history, dating back to the 1987-88 school year. The other recorded drop happened in the 2020-21 school year, during the height of the COVID-19 shutdowns. The enrollment drop is happening across the state, with only the Abilene area seeing an increase in enrollment, and only certain areas in central and east Texas holding steady. The biggest drops are taking place in south and west Texas, with the Midland, Amarillo, Edinburg, and San Angelo regions all losing at least 2.5% of their student population. "(The decline is) spread out across all types of students, it's spread out across all areas of the state," Mary Lynn Pruneda , the Director of Education and Workforce Policy for Texas 2036, said. "So that makes it really hard to point to one particular thing and say, 'Yes, this is definitely the reason that there are fewer kids in public schools today.' Schools are also disproportionately losing Hispanic and White students. While the overall public school population dropped 1.4%, the Hispanic population dropped by 2.1% and the White population dropped by 1.9%. Overall, Hispanic students made up 81% of the loss enrollment loss. The data also shows declines in traditionally underserved communities -- with homeless students dropping by 8% and economically disadvantaged students dropping by 2.3%. () " CBP axes plan to build portion of border wall in Big Bend National Park" via -- A top U.S. Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) official told the Washington Examiner that plans to build a 30-foot-tall border wall in Big Bend National Park have been axed. CBP Commissioner Rodney Scott told the Examiner it would be "kind of silly" to put a border wall on top of the park's towering granite cliffs. Instead of the physical barrier, Scott said officials will pave roads along the border of the national park and utilize drones and other digital surveillance equipment. "So what we're trying to convey is that we are going to have meaningful border security in that entire area," Scott said. () " Excessive heat suspected as cause of death after six bodies found in rail car near Laredo" via Garcia and Alex Nguyen - Extreme heat is suspected to have played a role in the deaths of six people from Mexico and Honduras whose bodies were discovered inside a train car in Laredo. A 29-year-old woman from Mexico and a 24-year-old man from Honduras were among the six deceased individuals found inside a shipping container at Union Pacific Railyard on Sunday afternoon, according to Webb County officials. The other four individuals were all male and included one teenager, though their identities had not yet been confirmed. The Webb County Medical Examiner determined that the woman died due to hyperthermia, or overheating. Hyperthermia is also suspected to have caused the death of the other five individuals, though formal examinations for them are still pending, according to a news release issued by the county. Corinne Stern , the county's medical examiner, found identification cards and cellphones that indicated the individuals were from Mexico and Honduras, according to the Associated Press. Their fingerprints were also shared with the U.S. Border Patrol to help confirm their identities and nationalities through the Missing Alien Program. () " Report reveals how much water could be consumed by Texas data centers" via Michael Garcia - Texas' booming data center industry could strain the state's already stressed water supply, with facilities projected to account for up to 9% of statewide water use by 2040, according to a University of Texas study. The report, which accounted for water used for cooling and to produce the needed power at data centers, comes as many data centers are planned throughout the state. With researchers at UT saying there are more than 400 data centers operating or under construction in Texas, they're urging for more transparency, improved planning and alternative water sources to reduce pressure on supplies, the study states. Currently, data centers account for less than 1% of the state's water use. "There's a lot of uncertainty surrounding the water use for data centers," said Mariam Arzumanyan , a fellow at the Bureau of Economic Geology at UT Austin's Jackson School of Geosciences, in a written statement. "People don't know the scale of how much water is going to be needed. There is not a unified understanding of the technologies used for cooling, or how much water that technology would use." () " Gas power leapfrogs wind for first time in 10 years in Texas' grid connection queue" via Brandon Mulder - A decade ago, wind power was surging in popularity and attracting huge investments that made Texas a national leader in renewable energy. But today, gas generation is making a big comeback, driven by a wave of data centers flooding into the state. For the last six months, the volume of gas generation in the Texas grid's interconnection queue -- the yearslong waiting list for electric generators wanting to connect to the grid -- has surpassed wind. It's the first time since January 2016 that gas has overtaken wind in the queue, a shift that reflects the policy and economic headwinds facing the wind industry and data centers favoring gas power as they seek to cash in on the artificial intelligence boom. "The data center explosion and their desire for 24/7 power probably excited a lot of gas developers, and that gas queue got bigger," said University of Texas professor of energy regulation David Spence. Like every power grid operator in the U.S., the Electric Reliability Council of Texas, or ERCOT, uses the interconnection queue to manage and plan for new power generation coming online. But not all projects in the queue ultimately reach completion. According to the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, or LBNL, only 22% of projects in ERCOT's queue actually get built, which is still the highest percentage of any grid in the nation. () " Houston's fastest-growing suburb is quietly sinking" via Molly Wilhelm \-- Katy--located west of Houston and long-ranked among the state's fastest-expanding communities--is sinking faster than any other suburb in the Houston area, according to a recent report from the Houston-Galveston Subsidence District. Over roughly the last two decades, Katy has sunk approximately 14 inches, according to the report. Between 2021 and 2025, the Houston-Galveston Subsidence District recorded an average annual subsidence rate of about one inch in Katy. The organization defines subsidence as the sinking of the Earth's surface due to subsurface movement. "There is still ongoing subsidence, particularly in western Harris County in the Katy and Fulshear areas, with some rates showing over two centimeters per year," Ashley Greuter , the district's director of research and water conservation, said during a presentation of the report in late April. () 2026 " State of Texas: Poll shows Cornyn, Paxton in tight runoff race for Republican U.S. Senate nomination" via Adam Schwager - Voters are just a few weeks away from a runoff election that could signal a major shakeup in Texas politics. The runoff will determine whether incumbent U.S. Senator John Cornyn will get the chance to defend his seat in the November election. New polling shows a tight race between Cornyn and Attorney General Ken Paxton. The Hobby School of Public Affairs at the University of Houston surveyed 1,200 likely Republican runoff voters between April 28 and May 1. The results show Paxton with 48% support and 45% support for Cornyn. The margin of error for the poll is +/- 2.83%. Mark P. Jones , political science fellow at Rice University's Baker Institute for Public Policy and a senior research fellow at the Hobby School, noted that Paxton picked up a notably larger share of the support from voters who cast a ballot in March for third-place finisher Wesley Hunt , with 53% of Hunt voters backing Paxton and 34% opting for Cornyn in the runoff. With both candidates running neck-and-neck, an endorsement from President Trump could change the entire race. "Trump set a precedent with his endorsement of (Republican Comptroller nominee) Don Huffines and (incumbent Agriculture Commissioner) Sid Miller back in March, where he was willing to wait until the last day of early voting... until dawn on Election Day, May 26, we can't actually rule out a Donald Trump endorsement," Jones said. () " Former President Obama makes surprise stop in Austin with James Talarico, Gina Hinojosa" via John C. Moritz - Former President Barack Obama appeared alongside U.S. Senate candidateJames Talarico and gubernatorial candidate Gina Hinojosa on Tuesday in Austin as part of an attempt to boost a new crop of Democratic candidates ahead of this year's midterms. The appearance was not a formal endorsement, but Obama introduced the two to a crowd of awestruck lunch goers at a taco restaurant east of the University of Texas as "the next senator and governor of Texas." Democrats haven't won a statewide contest in Texas in 32 years. "Now everybody remember to vote," the former president said as the young crowd jockeyed for photos and pleaded for autographs. () " Immigration a flashpoint in Allred-Johnson Democratic runoff" via Olivia Borgula -- As he campaigned for the Senate in 2024, then-U.S. Rep. Colin Allred sought to appeal to a wide range of voters, many of whom were dissatisfied with the Biden administration's border policies. He ran an ad standing side by side with law enforcement that touted him as "tough" and "standing up to extremists in both parties." He broke from Democrats on multiple immigration bills, including the Laken Riley Act, which required no-bond detention for undocumented immigrants accused of certain crimes, including lower-level offenses like shoplifting. Two years later, Allred is running for Congress again, but this time in a solidly blue, Dallas-centered seat. He's now calling to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement and denouncing for-profit immigration enforcement -- positions that prompted his primary runoff opponent, Rep. Julie Johnson , to label him a "flip-flopper." Allred's changed campaign focus is emblematic of a broader shift among Democrats in a vastly different political climate under President Donald Trump. His administration's immigration raids and mass deportations have sparked outrage among many Democrats who spent the Biden era playing defense on immigration. () " Christian Menefee, Alex Mealer lead Houston-area congressional runoffs, new poll finds" via Gabby Birenbaum -- Rep.Christian Menefee l eads Rep.Al Green by 7 percentage points heading into the final days of the runoff, according to a new poll of the closely watched race between two Houston Democratic members of Congress. The University of Houston's Hobby School of Public Affairs polled likely voters in two Houston-area contests -- the heavily Democratic 18th Congressional District, where Green and Menefee are running, and the red-leaning 9th Congressional District's Republican runoff between state Rep. Briscoe Cain , R-Deer Park, and Army veteran Alex Mealer. In the 18th District, the poll found Menefee garnering 50% of the vote to Green's 43%. The poll was conducted from May 5 to 8 and included a sample of 800 likely voters. It has a margin of error of +/-3.46 percentage points. The two are running against one another after Texas GOP legislators redrew the state's congressional map last summer, moving the 9th District, which Green has represented for over 20 years, to new territory that favors the GOP, and in the process putting a large share of Green's current constituents into the new 18th District. () " Harris County Treasurer Carla Wyatt's latest arrest adds to growing legal troubles during re-election campaign" via Jung -- Harris County Treasurer Dr. Carla Wyatt is facing legal trouble again after being arrested for driving while intoxicated in Galveston County over the weekend. According to Galveston County jail records, Wyatt was arrested Saturday on a DWI charge and later released on a $3,000 bond. KPRC 2 has learned she was arrested in Texas City. The arrest marks Wyatt's second DWI arrest and her third arrest since taking office as Harris County Treasurer. Court records show Wyatt was previously arrested for DWI in Houston in December 2023. () STATE GOVERNMENT " Texas truckers struggle after noncitizen licenses canceled" via Colleen DeGuzman and Alex Nguyen - Veronica Viera loved watching Texas unfold from the driver's seat of her bright pink 18-wheeler -- the winding roads, the small towns, the sense of freedom -- so losing her license in a government crackdown on legal immigrants was devastating. No more trips to and from Houston, listening to pop and Christian music. No more hauling whiskey from Laredo, tangerines from Brownsville, solar panels to the Hill Country. Viera's life abruptly changed when Texas, following the dictates of the Trump administration, canceled commercial driver's licenses, or CDLs, held by legally present noncitizens, including asylum seekers, refugees and DACA recipients. Texas was one of the first states to take action. She heard about the cancellations in December as men unloaded office chairs she'd hauled to San Antonio in the beloved semi she named Pink Panther. () #TXLEGE " Could Texas eliminate school property taxes? What to know" via Scott Huddleston -** With deadlines quickly approaching for Texans to protest their property value appraisals, school districts are starting to forecast how changing values will affect their budgets. Texas schools are funded by two main pots of money. The state determines how much funding it takes to educate each district's students, accounting for special student needs like dyslexia services or career and technical education courses. Each year, school districts levy a local property tax to raise money to pay for their budgets. Some districts with higher property values are able to fund their entire budget out of this local tax revenue. But districts with lower property tax values may still need more support to fill their coffers. That's where the state comes in -- kicking in funding to make districts whole. () LOCAL GOVERNMENT " Fort Worth to review plans for $10 billion data center development" via Emily Holshouser - The Fort Worth City Council is expected to review the site plan for a data center Tuesday, May 12, planned for the city's southeast edge that has brought concern to residents and some leaders. Black Mountain, a Fort Worth-based energy consortium, has hit roadblocks in the development of an AI data center project after successfully petitioning the city to rezone roughly 431 acres near Forest Hill and Everman. On Tuesday, the council will review a 187-acre site plan for the development that the zoning commission recommended approval for in April. The site, at the corner of Lon Stephenson Road and Forest Hill Drive, was initially rezoned in 2025. The site plan includes a 70-foot increase in the setback against Lon Stephenson Road, putting the edge of the campus 150 feet from single-family residential zoning, and an increase in the allowed height of the buildings on the site from 55 feet to 70 feet. () " Austin leaders push for faster action on troubled 911 system" via Austin Sanders - The 911 Communications Center at the Austin Police Department on Thursday, September 14, 2023. Austin City Council members pressed public safety officials Tuesday for answers on why the city is months behind on a plan to consolidate emergency communications, warning that the delays leave residents in some parts of the city with less reliable 911 services. At a special-called meeting of the City Council's Public Safety Committee, officials provided an update on the city's progress on an initiative to integrate 911 call-taking and dispatch functions into one centralized department, but Krista Laine and other council members balked at the lack of progress on a project ordered in August. Laine, who introduced the original resolution calling for the consolidated emergency communications center, said Tuesday's presentation was delivered months late and fell far short of what City Council requested. () " Texas school districts face first deadline from law requiring seat belts on buses" via Beasley - The first deadline for a new Texas law on school bus safety is approaching. Senate Bill 546, which passed during the 2025 regular legislative session, requires all public school buses to have three-point seat belts by 2029. Three-point seat belts include a shoulder belt and a lap belt, as opposed to a two-point belt, which only goes across the lap. While the deadline to install the belts is still years away, districts must report to the TEA how much it will cost them to retrofit or replace their buses by May 29. That includes buses operated by or contracted for use by the school district. The Legislature did not provide funding for the mandate; school boards may either comply by using district funds, or they may approve an exemption if funding is not available. () " Webb County Sheriff Martin Cuellar faces removal attempt following federal fraud indictment" via Alex Nguyen - Nearly six months after being indicted on federal fraud charges, Webb County Sheriff Martin Cuellar is now facing an attempt to remove him from office. Former Laredo City Council member Alfonso "Poncho" Casso filed the petition to remove Cuellar in Webb County district court last week, citing the federal indictment and other misconduct allegations. Casso's filing, which was first reported by The Laredo Morning Times, asked the court to suspend the five-term South Texas sheriff from office pending a trial that seeks to permanently remove him from the post. Cuellar denied all allegations outlined in the petition and "demands strict proof," according to a response filed in court on Friday. He already pleaded not guilty to the federal charges, which were unsealed in January. Casso's petition largely relies on the five-count indictment, which accuses Cuellar and two other people of misappropriating funds from the Webb County sheriff's office during the COVID-19 pandemic. () " Texas city ousts top attorney amid backlash over local election changes" via Nicholas Hernandez - New Braunfels officials voted Monday night to remove City Attorney Valeria Acevedo after a week of fallout tied to the city's mayoral election, creating uncertainty around the city's leadership just weeks before a scheduled runoff. In a 4-3 decision, the City Council sided with Mayor Pro Tem Lawrence Spradley and councilmembers Michael Capizzi , Lee Edwards and Mayor Neal Linnartz to terminate Acevedo. Councilmembers Toni Carter , Mary Ann Labowski and April Ryan voted against the move. The decision follows confusion surrounding the May 2 mayoral race, where early results showed challenger Michael French leading with less than 50% of the vote. While the city charter appeared to allow a candidate to win by plurality, officials later determined that state law requires a majority in races with terms longer than two years, forcing a runoff. That reversal, which came days after initial results were announced, drew criticism from residents and scrutiny over how the inconsistency went unnoticed. The issue was ultimately flagged by outside legal counsel, prompting the city to reassess the election outcome before it was finalized. () BUSINESS NEWS " Tesla heads off trial in Gigafactory Texas assault case tied to Austin mass shooting" via Guzm an - Gigafactory Texas in Austin is seen Thursday. A lawsuit over an alleged assault late last year at the sprawling factory has been moved to private arbitration by a state District Court judge. Tesla employee Lillian Brady speaks in March about her allegation that co-worker Ndiaga Diagne assaulted her at Gigafactory Texas on Dec. 4, months before he carried out a mass shooting at Buford's Backyard Beer Garden on West Sixth Street. Tesla Inc. has successfully fended off a public trial over a Gigafactory Texas assault case tied to the former employee suspected in a mass shooting in March on West Sixth Street. The Austin company was granted a motion for arbitration, avoiding a trial the alleged victim said she hoped would shed light on Tesla's missed opportunities to stop the assault that left three people dead and 15 injured. () " 300+ cases filed so far in new Texas business court and experts say more are coming" via Dylan McKim \-- State leaders were quick to take credit after Dell Technologies announced last week it plans to reincorporate its business in the Lone Star State where it is already headquartered. State Rep. Jeff Leach , R - Plano, posted on his X account following the Dell announcement, 'It's a direct result of the work we've been doing to strengthen our business climate'. Gov. Greg Abbott celebrated the news on his X account saying 'more businesses are sure to follow'; The move by Dell will not affect any operations or move any new employees to Texas but the move signals a result of the changes made to the state's corporate laws. For years, Texas lagged behind other states like Delaware that had more business-friendly laws and sophisticated business courts that attracted millions of companies to incorporate within its borders. Incorporating in a state -- or making it your legal home -- means the company's internal affairs are governed by that state's specific laws. It is not uncommon for companies to operate in one state but be incorporated in another. In the past two legislative sessions in Austin, lawmakers were able to finally create and expand the Texas Business Court and lowered corporate accountability. The courts started hearing cases in September 2024. Between 2024 and 2025 the state saw a 12% increase in the number of out-of-state limited liability companies that filed to do business in Texas, according to data from the Texas Secretary of State's (SOS) office. It's hard to determine if that increase is due to changes at the legislative level, but a spokesperson for the SOS said the increase was consistent with long-term growth in the state. The Texas Business Court consists of 11 divisions of judges that have specific expertise in complex business cases. The judges are appointed by the governor and serve two-year terms. Currently only five divisions are operating and they all encompass Texas's urban areas. Brad Foster , a partner at Haynes Boone, said creating a specialized court in Texas for business disputes was necessary. In the past, Texas-based companies would sometimes have to leave the state for disputes if they were not incorporated here. "You could have a dispute between two Dallas or Houston based people and they would be having to go to Delaware, hire Delaware lawyers and litigate their dispute -- that really is only a Texas dispute -- up there," Foster explained. | | | Dear Friend,

I’m running for San Mateo County Assessor-County Clerk-Recorder & Chief Elections Officer to bring trusted leadership, accountability, and responsive public service to one of the county’s most important offices.

[](https://us.list-manage.com/Gnh3qzHZbxR?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02)

This office impacts residents every single day, from ensuring fair property assessments and maintaining vital public records to protecting secure, accessible, and transparent elections. I’m committed to modernizing operations, restoring public trust, and delivering the professionalism and service San Mateo County residents deserve.

[DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/qrb8q1MNAmN?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02)

As a former Mayor and current member of the Board of Supervisors, I oversee a $5.5 billion organization with 5,800 employees and strong financial reserves. I understand the importance of transparency, sound management, and delivering reliable services that people can count on.
Now, with our critical May 16 fundraising deadline quickly approaching, I’m asking for your support.

Every contribution helps us expand voter outreach, share our message across San Mateo County, and build the grassroots campaign needed to win this important race. We cannot afford to slow down at this critical moment.

Please make a contribution today and help us keep our momentum strong:

[DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/DRYvIYXhAWT?e=c0babbc643&c2id=bfcaacdd1ef4033edfed3d4b1d472a02)

Thank you for your support, your encouragement, and your belief in leadership that puts San Mateo County residents first.

With gratitude,

David Canepa
San Mateo County Supervisor

P.S. The May 16th deadline is one of the most important moments of our campaign so far. Every donation made before midnight helps us reach more voters and build the momentum needed to win.

---
Derek, The midterms are less than six months away, and now more than ever, **we need a strong Democratic Party.** [**Today, we’re asking for your help to keep building it.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-may-2026-mid-month?amount=7&refcode=em_20260514_7115_fr&refcode2=7115_22930333_PMG8GV&akid=7115%2E22930333%2EPMG8GV)** But before we ask for your support, we want to explain where your $3 goes when you donate to the DNC. Since the start of this year, we’ve:
* Launched our _When We Count_ program, which trains new Democratic organizers and registers new Democratic voters in key battleground states.
* Released our 2026 Playbook, a comprehensive guide for state parties and campaigns that includes resources and best practices they’ll need to run winning organizing programs this year and beyond.
* AND we’ve sued the Trump administration over his executive order attempting to create eligible voter lists in each state and allowing him to decide who gets to vote by mail.

clean_body: Register as a Republican, Request your vote by mail ballot, see if you are in the new district, and help us phone bank! | | | | | == | AMERICA FIRST. NAVY VETERAN. PROVEN LEADER. | Dear Peter, I have officially filed to run in the new Republican majority Florida Congressional District 25! The Republican Primary is on Tuesday, August 18. Please take a moment to complete the following steps to help me win, by clicking the blue boxes below: 1. Register as a Republican, so you can vote for me in the primary. 2. | Friend,
In the past few weeks, MAGA has unleashed a blitzkrieg in the courts. Two decisions in particular should send a chill down every American's spine.
The Supreme Court ruled that Alabama can suspend an ongoing election to rush through a gerrymandered map. This came after the same court threw out a challenge to Texas' illegal racially gerrymandered maps -- ruling it was too close to an election for the courts to intervene. That Texas decision came in December. Months before the primary. In Virginia, the MAGA-packed state Supreme Court went even further -- overruling the results of a statewide redistricting referendum where millions of voters went to the polls and a majority said yes. Read that again. A court just overruled the results of an election.

Democrats cannot unilaterally disarm while MAGA uses packed courts to rig the system against us. We have to fight back. In the coming days, Defend Our Courts will announce a major new initiative aimed at Supreme Court reform. But right now, we are laser focused on one thing: Georgia votes on May 19th.
Jen Jordan and Miracle Rankin are running against the two MAGA justices who shielded Trump from criminal accountability when he tried to steal Georgia's 2020 election. A win lays the foundation to flip that court entirely just months before the 2028 presidential election.

| | | Friend, Our latest fundraising numbers have me so worried that I immediately typed this letter to every single top grassroots conservative we have on file. _The situation is that desperate._ **With the May end-of-month deadline rapidly approaching, we 're still far short ****of our crucial fundraising goal.** This goal isn't just some arbitrary number that I landed on. We need every last donor to compete with the _BILLIONS_ that Democrats are spending to BUY the midterm elections. **_... ## Texas Has Nation's Fastest-Growing Cities
Texas is home to the nation's five fastest-growing cities with populations of at least 20,000, according to U.S. Census Bureau estimates released yesterday. The [report](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGypCAURVeDGRa8FsGAYBKzP-mE1mt4rVShWPBGf-9-qmcLfwP3nnP-fC1fmHI61t-4k-fvV1kOulsmZqrLCxtT47WWOx1rSJyohbITL6BglMpIbZaIKb-XoYv-qeKkO_LaWucGmKzrNo-gNQ7OPYyzGCI-XYhhotFOiE-EoUv-M6aMNlorMLZ3BqJ6OEUYyBo9ikFRTFxqzxsxfWN75Xe5qPah7F32G_PZxOOXgFnAfN93H-hof1u_lkvA_PGppewC5rNSa7JSJmzUBMyfZwHzlQ7GlSQoMDIkfksu9yHPckpqnHZkav3Ge-6qj-edck5ttGJQ644p_8fgn8W7PPwLAAD__-nChYo) examined the period between July 2024 and July 2025. Four of the top five are in Collin County, while the Houston suburb of Fulshear claimed the No. 2 spot with a growth rate of 21%. Celina's 24.6% rate of growth ranked No. 1, while Princeton ranked No. 3 at 18.1%. Melissa and Anna [rounded out](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO5CAMgOGnIR0jcEKAIsU16fbaKyMHzAwSCSOwNrtvf5q9eYMrLUu__PnPx_aBueTz_hsPWvgr1e2kqxdiprYl7Eyd761e-byHzJl6qAfxBgpmqYzUZouYy_c2DXHZVfR6oEVb69wE3rrhsSStDOxJ2ThqO4L3IQS7B5tMmJyf45CXV0wZbbRWYOzNGYhqdIowkDV6FpOimLm2Gz-I6Qt7Kt_1k9ot1GMoy4P52cX4S8AqYL2u63YlxNdSwIqNcygkYH25BKylBiyvsTZ-yJ-cfDvlGyr_SWWgkk-Uz5bPQFxPeVDJvaPE80QBKzgrR632cTdBAiDKyYcoPaVZauOdt7T7hG5oS3xeuZTcZysmdT8wl5_j-f9e_rnA3wAAAP__iaiVwA) the top five, with growth rates of 14.5% and 10.2%, respectively. Some smaller cities [grew even faster](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDtygzAQhk8jOhhp0cuFijR0TpuSUWDBOxGIQRtjbp_BV0j9v-b_vu79PVKidf6MCwZ-Tblf8SgJmXHvp1gYC897PmidB2LCMuQFuQcJtpamVqYfI6Wz19UYvuV4UxUG5Zz3Gm7OV4-gjdeoW2sVqNi2CIMCOzllpW3B31xF4SqTRhmlJBjXeAOjbL3EOKAzygotcSTOe8MPZHzFMqUzP3FvhrxUKTyYtyLaDwGdgO44jubnFddLFNBdbwR075iADiSYeiA-6y1vvyky5bXGwrRExstQ7WHcDkqJinVCy3mJlN5D_D88zwB_AQAA___483i8), including Niederwald (65.3%), Lavon (45.3%), Crandall (36.4%), and Waller (35%). The Census Bureau's report highlighted how growth rates for large cities have slowed across the country, while suburbs have [maintained](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCnMR1obXDsFC7-hi5_eyVa7AUsGTvCqyS8_Sl3eYPrR6P55us23TCmmNf_uJPj11KmTM-aiJmOacHKVHk9yjPm1UeOVH3ZiScF6tKCbqWeAsZ0TkMT3AzhKhty0hhrB3U1ttmcsnbGnjAob_UCBvoFZ0Kjey_tTLaJ7l0GWmopQWnTWa0C9BYIPRktL2IACpHL0fFGTC-sSzrLg47Ol71JbmO-V9H_E2oUalxixuypO3Er5Z0QaiRfctlPoUY8OPpEVahRtx9e-_G1v8A2I8eSWxhAAhgpu4331Bwu3J8xpVgvRgyw7hjTzwD-220Pp74DAAD__7Vngts) a relatively stable rate of growth. In terms of raw numbers, six of the cities with the largest population increases are also in Texas: Fort Worth (No. 2), San Antonio (No. 3), Celina (No. 4), Houston (No. 6), Fulshear (No. 7), and McKinney (No. 10). Finally, Austin [topped](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3SAQhJ8GdxwBNgdcUKRxd9OmtLiwtlfCxmL3_L195OQRbjufZjQzf77mr4gFj_V33CHwe6nzAS8qwAxtXiIxEK-tvvBYEzICpboDz0aZu1RWajvniOUzD10O3yqPuoOgnfN-MKPz3RbcEnOyYx7B994NetCDTWMPCbzL_dJ3GK4wZbXVWhnrbt6arHqvICZwVt_FoCAj13bjDRjekZbyqU9ot1T3roSN-STR_xJmEmZK3xQfxHhcVJjpmiPMVGqKRZjpPyN51vNRImM9JD3aGYmApJY7lnJpDQgzHExyqU3yBnLBRiwZd5B4yA2Ja_t0LeTzdXno7sSg1j1i-VeLf3bmM5i_AQAA__869Y08) 1 million residents for the first time, becoming one of a dozen U.S. cities to surpass that threshold.
## Residents, Lawmakers Oppose Power Lines
Residents and lawmakers are pushing back on proposals to build massive 765-kV transmission lines from North, Central, and South Texas to the Permian Basin, claiming they will destroy property values and exceed the intent of the legislation that [authorized](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0EGyoyAQxvHT6A4LiChZsJiNu8x2llYrjekqBAt6Yrz9q-QK7wK_r77_v8f8AIqUtr-wo-N3yHPCs0ZkxjIHqIyVt5JPSttKTFjXvCPPWupBSCOUmT1QvOa-9W6R_q5adGocre31fbTt0-kw9AjLEoYFgkLtLdibX7S_-8Ga0LfkPpg0yigltRk7a7SXNysRVhyNGppeoifOpeMnMr6hhnjlF5ZuzXsb3ZP5qM3tT6OnRk8VEiTOiXLBIxfuctkaPR0RkthzQYERVy60El_ixMriS4odLvH5Jv4nnxM2emqL88dJMVIdxqaX2w4Uv5v8u1Ivp38CAAD__7lpgPI) their construction. Earlier this month, residents from nearly two dozen counties attended a meeting with the State Office of Administrative Hearings to voice their opposition to a proposed 270-mile route from Somervell County to Howard County. "_Landowners are fighting so hard for something that's already theirs_ ," [said](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAURb9GOwygCFNQbGM3225pGHgKyVMm8GYc_37j_sJ2N7nJubnn5z7fXcK0r99uA0ufJc87HBWBCMq8uEpQaS35SPvqEyWoPm9As-RyZFwxoebgEp7z0Ab74OEmWrBCa2MGedOmjTbo0TyWEEz_cL3UXvlh9Fr2_tYbNejQJnvBuBJKCC6V7oySgfeGg_OglRibgUNIlEtHEQg-ri545jeUzuetRRuJnrXpvxo5NXI6jqM7Xcz5ahs5XXcaOblCySNckcDHPWNeTxZfJSCw8ioO2YXeK3u-amSCK8251rKLtGFbbHgeCTHVUTcDXzeX8G-d_ufsbeVvAAAA___s0YHG) retired firefighter Lance Trinque. On Monday, 25 legislators [wrote a letter](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ugzAURp_GbCD7gn8YPHRhS9eOyLGviVWDEb4JydtXbdUn6PoN39E5H5f54lJO2_LuVrT0jGXe8KwZifCYo6uElZajnGlbfKKE1ZcVaQYOquWyFXIOLuXXPDTBXnkYRYNWaG3MAKM2zc2GXitwPA5cGi_HUXHuojYiRhG1Mtcm2e8zLoUUgoPUnZEQeG84Oo9aCsUGjiFROTq6IeHT1Zhf5YFH58vaZHsj2ivr3xhMDKbad6H4-4ob-VzuoSvHwmD62yqDCYwQSuiBwSSFANVqJT8f7X737a_4HmK3h9gcNuxnyjlVpdnAl9Wl_AOl_6V6WPgKAAD__9gBfBg) to the Public Utilities Commission of Texas (PUCT), arguing that ERCOT previously indicated only two of the three proposed routes are needed by 2030, and "prioritizing transmission of energy produced by renewables does nothing to address a significant problem in the mix of electrical generation we currently have in our state." Interestingly, Chinese billionaire Sun Guangxin, whose plans to build a wind farm on land near Laughlin Air Force Base were halted due to national security concerns, has [filed a protest](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuszAURp_GbCD7BmNn8PDrl1CHpuqQqiMy9oVYMhjZtyF5-4q8QvfzfUc635fhYkMM6_xhFzT0mNKw4l4iEmEeJlsIC8057WGdXaCAxaUFaQAOXc1lLeTgbYjPoa28Gbk_iwqNUErrFs5KVzdzHvkoFQetlXLjNI3-ZDXX3dhJ6YSbqmCOMy6FFIKDVI2W4PlJc7QOlRQdazn6QCk3dEPChy1TfKY75salpYrmRrQVdvrHoGfQv4DiUkZnsz8QBv2-1S6thCsx6H-2mKwvDPpDzKDnkkH_ZvMdC9XXY19_fv2_1u-vCs3mpyobv-0hxlA6xVo-LzbEl57-Fu1u4DcAAP__736BJA) with the PUCT over a proposed route near his residence that would cause "visual intrusion, long-term land use constraints, and potential reduction in property value."
## Solar Power to Surpass Coal
The U.S. Energy Information Administration [projects](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2uozAQQOGnMV3Q2PiPwsVKK7psuyVy8AAjGYzwKIS3v8oz3P7oK87_5_iMlGlf_sUNA3_mMu541YzMeI5zrIyVl7NctC8TMWGdyoY8KlD2AeYhzZgi5XvUTQovSL1sMEjnvNeqd75Zg9QQewOdfmljQKOP3vrUT9b6CeaUGgpfDIw0UoIyrvVGJeg8YJzQGWmFBkzE5Wx5RcZPrHO-yxvPdipbk8PKfFTR_RFqEGq4rqtFiu1S3kINXFK8accdz-UWakjIkXJ7rIfoBkqi-2ud9aY5QzouypmqdULDsn2rL8-_m_IO6icAAP__C6d1fw) that Texas-based solar power will generate 78 billion kilowatt-hours (BkWh) this year, compared to 60 BkWh for coal, marking the first time solar power exceeds coal's annual output on the ERCOT grid. Between 2021 and 2025, solar power's share of ERCOT's generation mix [increased](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOgzAQBNCvMR1obTAmhYtr6HLtlWhjL8SSwZG9Fyd_fyK_cP3Mk2Z-rssVQwzH9o07WX6taTmolkjMlJcVC1PhLacajs0FDlRc2okXBWpsQbdSLx5DfC9D4-0N_EU2ZKUx0zSoi5maux2gd6TWgTxqkBNqs4433_fGw6VHkE2wJwZaailBadNNWnnoJyB0ZLQcxQDkA6fc8Z2YXljW-E5Pyp1LexPtnflRRP8l1CzUXGvt1vQy-Fs4HGdEqPncJNT8KbclRcytSxhbyi5xk61_1BBjKKMRA2w7hvix-X-PPK36CwAA__-i43Zo) from 4% to 12%, while coal's share fell from 19% to 13%. Last year, solar power actually generated more electricity than coal did from March through August. There are currently no plans to build new coal power plants in Texas, while 14 BkWh in new solar capacity is expected to come online this year--representing 40% of all new solar capacity in the U.S.--followed by 11.8 BkWh next year. Derek, In just a minute, we’ll be asking you to [ **pitch in to the DNC before our mid-month deadline at midnight _tonight_.**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-may-2026-mid-month?amount=7&refcode=em_20260515_7142_fr&refcode2=7142_22930333_pwSUY-&akid=7142%2E22930333%2EpwSUY-) But first, we hope you’ll let us explain exactly where your donation goes: As Trump and his allies continue attacking our democracy and racing to cement their control of Congress ahead of this year’s midterms, it’s more important than ever that Democrats are not only able to cut through the noise, but to continue building the long-term infrastructure we’ll need to win back Congress this year and continue winning in years to come. **That’s what you’re powering when you donate to the DNC.** Just this year, we’ve:

* Sued the Trump administration to ensure that every American is able to make their voices heard at the ballot box this November.

**But here’s the thing, Derek: None of this work would be possible without the help of our grassroots supporters nationwide. Here’s what we have on record for you this year:** **_2026 DNC Supporter Record_** **Name:** Derek

| | Welcome back to Fact Check Friday. **Today, we're discussing the Energy Bills Relief Act and why I'm proud to cosponsor it!** It's abundantly clear that Republicans in Congress have no real desire to fix the suffering of millions of American families facing the affordability and energy crises — in fact, through their actions and policies, one could argue that they seem committed to making this crisis worse for hard-working Americans trying to make ends meet. I'm cosponsoring the Energy Bills Relief Act because El Pasoans are facing skyrocketing utility bills that force them to make heartbreaking choices between keeping the lights on, paying rent, or putting food on the table for their families. _I will not stand by while our community members are saddled with dramatic increases in utility bills just to subsidize energy-intensive data centers._ **So, what does the Energy Bills Relief Act do for Americans in need of support?**
* It reinstates the 2022 tax credits for home and energy-efficiency improvements, lowering families' monthly utility bills.
* It incentivizes utility companies to modernize their systems and pass those savings directly to consumers.
* It works with American families experiencing financial hardship to ensure they aren't left in the dark.
* It puts people before profit by cracking down on energy companies' attempting to price-gouge their customers.
* It ensures that facilities like data centers are paying for their own energy costs, instead of pushing expenses onto the rest of us.
* It gives a voice to the American people so they can benefit from energy projects in their community.

**For far too long, U.S. energy policy has focused on increasing the profits of energy corporations at the expense of hard-working American consumers.** The Energy Bills Relief Act is a bill that seeks to shift our focus back to solving the problems that most affect our communities, such as lowering costs and increasing reliability for American homes and businesses. _When we invest in clean energy, American families win._ Reliability and affordability shouldn't be luxuries. By expanding access to renewable energy, which is by far the most reliable and affordable energy source, we can finally break the cycle of skyrocketing bills and put power back in the hands and pockets of the people. Joining Steve is Robert L. Shibley Author and Executive director of the Foundation for Individual Rights in Education (FIRE). A native of Toledo, Ohio, he is a graduate of Duke University and Duke University School of Law. Robert is also the author of Twisting Title IX the story of how Title IX, a 1972 law intended to ban sex discrimination in education, became a monster that both the federal government and many college administrators treat as though it supersedes both the U.S. Constitution and hundreds of years of common law. It's a story about the victims of this law--men and women both--and of the unaccountable government bureaucrats at the Departments of Education and Justice who repeatedly prioritize an extreme brand of politics over free speech, fundamental fairness, and basic human decency.
Over the last 13 years, Robert has aided students and faculty members at hundreds of colleges and universities. He has discussed free speech and due process issues in national and international radio and TV interviews, including The O'Reilly Factor and CNN Tonight with Don Lemon, as well as in published op-eds in USA Today, the Washington Post, and many other newspapers and magazines. Robert and his wife Araz live in North Carolina with their two daughters. For more about Robert you can visit him at [www.fire.org](https://substack.com/redirect/e51cc22d-75d0-4fc6-8eaa-06aae7cff281?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Shibley Author and Executive director of the Foundation for Individual Rights in Education (FIRE). A native of Toledo, Ohio, he is a graduate of Duke University and Duke University School of Law. Robert is also the author of Twisting Title IX the story of how Title IX, a 1972 law intended to ban sex discrimination in education, became a monster that both the federal government and many college administrators treat as though it supersedes both the U.S. Constitution and hundreds of years of common law. It's a story about the victims of this law--men and women both--and of the unaccountable government bureaucrats at the Departments of Education and Justice who repeatedly prioritize an extreme brand of politics over free speech, fundamental fairness, and basic human decency. Over the last 13 years, Robert has aided students and faculty members at hundreds of colleges and universities. He has discussed free speech and due process issues in national and international radio and TV interviews, including The O'Reilly Factor and CNN Tonight with Don Lemon, as well as in published op-eds in USA Today, the Washington Post, and many other newspapers and magazines. Robert and his wife Araz live in North Carolina with their two daughters. [The U.S. Supreme Court just ruled that people can keep getting mifepristone by mail and at their local pharmacy—for now.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/131437486/621117311/1824768205?sourceid=1151360&utm_campaign=26emama-0502mdx-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=lavfda&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTE4MDhlOC02MDUwLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=f05CyRn6-vDglwWADCMvkBb86RF03YxwMNj76xhW2QQ=&emci=6c9c6c21-ed4f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=de1808e8-6050-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

And neither are we.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/131437488/621117318/1824768205?sourceid=1151360&utm_campaign=26emama-0502mdx-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=lavfda&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTE4MDhlOC02MDUwLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=f05CyRn6-vDglwWADCMvkBb86RF03YxwMNj76xhW2QQ=&emci=6c9c6c21-ed4f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=de1808e8-6050-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237) | [DEFEND ABORTION CARE](https://click.everyaction.com/k/131437490/621117324/1824768205?sourceid=1151360&utm_campaign=26emama-0502mdx-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=lavfda&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTE4MDhlOC02MDUwLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=f05CyRn6-vDglwWADCMvkBb86RF03YxwMNj76xhW2QQ=&emci=6c9c6c21-ed4f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=de1808e8-6050-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

Here's what happened: Earlier this month, the Fifth Circuit sided with Louisiana and reinstated a medically unnecessary requirement that mifepristone be dispensed in person, threatening access by mail and at pharmacies nationwide. The Supreme Court paused that order. Today, it extended that pause while the case continues.

[This back-and-forth has already caused real chaos for providers and patients. It won't stop here.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/131437492/621117331/1824768205?SelectedFrequency=0&sourceid=1151360&utm_campaign=26emama-0502mdx-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=lavfda&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTE4MDhlOC02MDUwLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=f05CyRn6-vDglwWADCMvkBb86RF03YxwMNj76xhW2QQ=&emci=6c9c6c21-ed4f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=de1808e8-6050-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

Medication abortion accounts for more than 60% of abortions in the U.S. each year. More than 7.5 million people have used mifepristone safely. Hundreds of studies back it. [Restricting it is not about safety—it's about making abortion as difficult, expensive, and unreachable as possible.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/131437494/621117337/1824768205?SelectedFrequency=0&sourceid=1151360&utm_campaign=26emama-0502mdx-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=lavfda&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZTE4MDhlOC02MDUwLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=f05CyRn6-vDglwWADCMvkBb86RF03YxwMNj76xhW2QQ=&emci=6c9c6c21-ed4f-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=de1808e8-6050-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

The people hit hardest: those with low incomes. People in rural areas, hours from the nearest clinic. People with disabilities. People escaping domestic violence.
