name: Office of U.S. Senator Angela Alsobrooks
subject: Senator Alsobrooks Newsletter -- May 15, 2026
body:
|

---
Dear Friends and Neighbors, Yesterday, in collaboration with my colleagues, we moved the CLARITY Act out of the Banking Committee and onto the Senate Floor. What we know is that the digital revolution is upon us, and it has presented a clear opportunity to support small businesses, generate wealth, spur innovation, and support younger Americans who want to be part of this revolution. In fact, I learned about crypto by listening to [my daughter and her friends talking](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15426.18332830.6144832.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fSen_Alsobrooks%2fstatus%2f2055120119819362332%3fs%3d20&redir_log=057634274064360), something that inspired me to take action when I came to the Senate. And it's clear that this digital revolution is happening with us or without us--we have a responsibility to regulate it to create rules of the road. That is why I've been at the table. I've been in negotiations for over nine months, working toward regulating digital assets in a way that protects consumers and reduces the risks of deposit flight and deceptive marketing. I have negotiated in good faith with colleagues on both sides of the aisle willing to meet this critical moment. I've worked to make this bill better.
Let me be very clear: my vote this week is a vote to keep working in good faith. It does not mean I will be voting for the passage of the CLARITY Act on the floor. We still have work to do.

We need to find a workable way to address law enforcement's concerns about financial crimes. I am a former prosecutor and know how important that is. We also need to include an agreement on ethics--that would apply not just to the President and Vice President but to all of us. The American people--especially my constituents--expect that from us. I will keep working with my colleagues to get this done.

Be clear, I believe that it is my responsibility-- my duty as your Senator-- to try and be at every table where consequential decisions are being made. Decisions that will affect all of us in one way or another. As they say, if you're not at the table, you're on the menu. So, I have worked to do my level best to include protections for American consumers, and I'm not done yet.
Americans--from every background and every community--deserve to benefit financially from this digital revolution and be protected from the risks that come with it. If we don't act, we will be left behind. I won't let that happen.
**Fighting Through Legislation **
It's been a busy two weeks here on the Hill, and I have been fighting to deliver for Marylanders in the Senate. From women's health to protecting workers to expanding broadband access in Appalachia, I introduced and cosponsored legislation that I feel will help support Maryland families. _These are the bills I introduced: _

HBCU Arts Act: This bipartisan bill would amend Section 323 of the Higher Education Act of 1965 to expand permissible uses of federal Strengthening HBCUs Program grant funding to include support for arts, arts education, and cultural programs. New allowable uses include financial assistance to arts students; outreach and development offices for arts departments; wrap‐around services (mentorship, counseling, career advising); exhibition and preservation of Black art collections; and paid internships, apprenticeships, and fellowship opportunities in collaboration with nonprofit and cultural institutions. It also authorizes partnerships with the National Endowment for the Arts and broadly defines "arts" to include performance, literary, visual, graphic, plastic, and decorative forms.

Financial Access Protection Act: This bill would prohibit banks from "collecting, maintaining, and disclosing" information tied to Americans' citizenship and immigration status.

_These are the bills I have cosponsored: _

Full-Service Community School Enhancement Act: This bill would invest $3.65 billion in the Full-Service Community Schools Program over the next five years to provide renewable grants for the planning, implementation, and expansion of community schools to meet the needs of students, families, and the communities they serve. It would also help states and communities build out the infrastructure to support this important model for public education and provide resources for technical assistance and sharing of best practices.

Advancing Menopause Care and Mid-Life Women's Health Act: This bill would expand federal research, public health education, provider training, care coordination, and Centers of Excellence focused on perimenopause, menopause, post menopause, and related mid-life women's health conditions. The bill authorizes funding for the NIH and public health research, grants to improve early detection and treatment, a national education and outreach program, health professional training, and reporting on disparities and barriers to care.

Fair Trusts for Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2026: This bill would address a persistent source of tax avoidance--wealthy families using complex trust structures to indefinitely defer estate, gift, and generation-skipping transfer tax liability. This legislation creates a progressive withholding tax on trust-held assets above $50 million, with rates scaling from 1% to 3% based on asset amount. The tax is fully refundable against future estate tax liability, the aggregate withholding is capped to not exceed the estate tax that would be owed, and charitable, ERISA-qualified, and other exempt trusts are not affected.

Terrorism Risk Insurance Program Reauthorization Act of 2026: This reauthorization would ensure insurance companies can offer coverage for terrorism-related damage. With the Terrorism Risk Insurance Act (TRIA), insurance companies can sell policies that include terrorism coverage, and if a very large attack occurs, the federal government helps cover part of the losses, preventing insurers from going bankrupt and keeping insurance available for businesses. This bill would reauthorize TRIA until 2034.

Protecting America's Workers Act: This bill would strengthen health and safety protections for workers by expanding Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Act coverage to public employees including federal, state, and local workers; imposing penalties for OSH Act violators, including criminal charges for egregious violators; protecting workers who report unsafe workplace conditions by aligning OSH Act whistleblower protections with more recently updated laws, like the protections within the Surface Transportation Act; mandating that DOL investigate all cases of workplace deaths or serious injuries; and requiring employers to inform workers of their rights under the OSH Act.

Protecting Human Rights and Public Health in Foreign Assistance Act: This bill would prohibit federal funding for implementation, administration, or enforcement of the Trump Administration's Promoting Human Flourishing in Foreign Assistance (PHFFA) Policy.

Puppy Protection Act of 2026: This bill would create stronger standards for veterinary care, housing, and breeding for dogs. Specifically, this legislation ensures that dogs in breeders' care have suitable and safe enclosures, outdoor areas, and regulated interactions with humans and other dogs.

Expanding Appalachia's Broadband Access Act: This bill would increase access to broadband for rural communities across Appalachia. This bill would direct the U.S. Government Accountability Office to study and measure the capabilities of satellites for rural business and services.

Federal Worker Credit Protection Act of 2026: This bill would prevent harm to credit ratings because of missed or delayed payments when federal workers aren't getting paychecks, helping ensure that federal workers are not financially penalized for circumstances beyond their control.

Holocaust Education and Antisemitism Lessons (HEAL) Act: This bill would direct the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum to study and report on Holocaust education efforts in states, local educational agencies (LEAs), and public elementary and secondary schools. Among other elements, the study must (1) determine whether states and LEAs require Holocaust education as part of the curriculum taught in public elementary and secondary schools, (2) identify the standards and requirements relating to Holocaust education, and (3) identify the types of instructional material used to teach students about the Holocaust. TAP Promotion Act: The bill would make sure that accredited representatives from Veterans Service Organizations (VSOs) are allowed to participate in transition assistance program (TAP) classes to help transitioning servicemembers file Benefits Delivery at Discharge (BDD) claims, since TAP classroom instructors aren't legally allowed to help fill out benefits paperwork.

A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against the Republic of Cuba that have not been authorized by Congress.

A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Industry and Security of the Department of Commerce relating to "One Year Suspension of Expansion of End-User Controls for Affiliates of Certain Listed Entities".

A resolution honoring the life of Dirk Arthur Kempthorne, former United States Senator for the State of Idaho. (Agreed to in the Senate!)

**In the Community **
I was honored to meet the crew of Artemis II and hear about their mission to the moon. It was especially exciting to speak with Reid Wiseman. We are so proud to see a Maryland native leading this era of space exploration.

Too many hardworking Americans come face to face with barriers preventing them from creating and building generational wealth. I joined Tiffany Haddish at the Milken Institute Global Conference to talk about how we can create pathways for true upward economic mobility.

I attended the Franklyn Bourne Bar Association Annual Scholarship Tea. This organization helped shape my journey and that of so many across Maryland. From a time when women were shut out of the law to today, we've made progress, but the fight for equity and justice continues.

I was happy to welcome small business leaders to the Hill for the Meta Small Business Conference. From expanding access to capital to cutting startup costs, we're working to ensure small businesses across Maryland can grow, compete, and thrive.

I met with the Daisies from Girl Scout Troop Fairylights and wow -- talk about big dreams! Their excitement and creativity gives me so much hope for the future.

Grateful to join the Southern Maryland Chapter Links, Inc. for an afternoon of sisterhood and celebration. In challenging times, their commitment to service, community, and lifting others up matters more than ever.
**Grant Spotlight **
I wanted to share a couple of grant opportunities for nonprofits, public, and private institutions that will go a long way to help Maryland students and families.
**_[Department of Health and Human Services Office of Elementary and Secondary Education Promise Neighborhoods-84.215N](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15426.18332830.6144832.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f362347&redir_log=352023644521340)_** is a Department of Education Program being administered at HHS. The purpose of the Promise Neighborhoods program is to significantly improve the academic and developmental outcomes of children and youth living in the most distressed communities of the United States, including ensuring school readiness, high school graduation, and access to a community-based continuum of high-quality services. The program serves neighborhoods with high concentrations of individuals with low incomes; multiple signs of distress, which may include high rates of poverty, childhood obesity, academic challenges, and juvenile delinquency, adjudication, or incarceration; and adverse childhood experiences; and also serves schools implementing comprehensive support and improvement activities or targeted support and improvement activities under section 1111(d) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, as amended (ESEA). All strategies in the continuum of solutions must be accessible to children with disabilities and English learners. (Posted May 11, 2026 - August 8, 2026 deadline) An institution of higher education, and non-profits working with a local educational agency, local government, or a tribal organization, are eligible to apply for this grant. _[**Department of Energy - Promise Neighborhoods Synopsis 2**](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15426.18332830.6144832.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.grants.gov%2fsearch-results-detail%2f362347&redir_log=352023644521340)_ is a Department of Education Program being administered at DOE and has as its purpose to significantly improve the academic and developmental outcomes of children and youth living in the most distressed communities of the United States, including ensuring school readiness, high school graduation, and access to a community-based continuum of high-quality services. The program serves neighborhoods with high concentrations of individuals with low incomes; multiple signs of distress, which may include high rates of poverty, childhood obesity, academic challenges, and juvenile delinquency, adjudication, or incarceration; and adverse childhood experiences. (Posted May 8, 2026 - August 6, 2026 deadline) An institution of higher education, and non-profits working with a local educational agency, local government, or a tribal organization, are eligible to apply for this grant. [Department of Education - **_Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS): Office of Special Education Programs (OSEP): Community Parent Resource Centers (CPRCs), Assistance Listing Number 84.328C Synopsis 2_**](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15426.18332830.6144832.7190525&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2foutreach.senate.gov%2fiqextranet%2fiqClickTrk.aspx%3f%26cid%3dSenHirono%26crop%3d14190.9068651.6032619.1059911%26report_id%3d%26redirect%3dhttps%253a%252f%252fwww.grants.gov%252fsearch-results-detail%252f361760%26redir_log%3d191857631719340&redir_log=953616158231492) funds programs to ensure that parents of children with disabilities receive high-quality, relevant, and useful training and information to help improve outcomes for their children. CPRCs must increase - parents' capacity to help their children (a) meet developmental and functional goals and challenging academic achievement goals that have been established for all children; and (b) be prepared to lead productive and independent adult lives, to the maximum extent possible. (Posted April 6, 2026 - June 5, 2026 deadline) **Georges Creek ** One year after devastating flooding in Georges Creek, we honor the resilience of the communities and everyone who stepped up to help rebuild. People came from all over Maryland and the region to support the recovery efforts. The strength of Georges Creek has carried this community forward, and we will continue standing with them every step of the way. **Stay in the Fight ** I know these are difficult times. But please know that I will continue fighting for you every step of the way. We will not give up. We will not give in to this Administration, and I ask that you continue to fight alongside us. Please continue to reach out to us. You can call the office or connect with us at [alsobrooks.senate.gov](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenAlsobrooks&crop=15426.18332830.6144832.7190525&report_id=&redirect=http%3a%2f%2falsobrooks.senate.gov%2f&redir_log=346519414955204). You can also follow us on Bluesky, Instagram, Facebook, Threads, YouTube, and X. We are in this TOGETHER. Sincerely, Angela D. Alsobrooks
United States Senator

body:
Campaign Newsletter | Issue 2, Volume 1

| | | | | [|
---](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=06b580024f&e=1030105c7f)
| | Newsletter | Issue 2, Volume 1 | May 15, 2026
---
| | Ericka Kopp (D) is running for Congress to unseat Rob Wittman (R)
in Virginia’s First District. On a platform of access and accountability through action, Ericka is the strong, progressive advocate we need in DC to fight for people-first policies.
---
| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
### VA-01, we never left
---
| | Source: February 8Press Release
---
| [Visit Source](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=d43b077bc5&e=1030105c7f)
---
| | | Before Virginia said yes to the referendum vote, we saw many congressional candidates commit to two districts under the (still) current and would-be district map. Ericka could not and would not make that decision in advance of the people’s vote and the court’s decision. She said in a press release dated February 8, 2026,
_“I respect the decision of the people. Their voice being heard is what matters most. That is why I’m running for Congress. Until Virginians vote to redistrict, the first district has my heart and my full attention. Every Virginian deserves to feel heard and to have a representative who fights for them.”_
VA-01, you are home. Your residents are like extended family. Ericka Kopp and her team are honored to serve you in Congress.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
### Vote for Ericka by August 4
---
| | Source: Virginia Dept. of Elections
---
| [Visit Source](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=f61da6aa7f&e=1030105c7f)
---
| | |
With the primary election approaching, here are the key dates to keep in mind:

**August 4, 2026 - Primary**

**Vote by Mail (Absentee)**

* Apply for a ballot to be mailed to you through Friday, July 24, 2026

**Early In-Person Voting**
* Starts: Thursday, June 18, 2026
(in observation of Juneteenth on Friday)
* Ends: Saturday, August 1, 2026

**Voter Registration**
* Register to vote or update your registration by Friday, July 24, 2026

Polling places and more information can be found at [elections.virginia.gov](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=9a52cb445b&e=1030105c7f).
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
### Ericka has the fire to represent VA-01
---
| | Source: May 12 Wittman Watch
---
| [Visit Source](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=2ebe91f87b&e=1030105c7f)
---
| | | [Wittman Watch](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=96d14ecc06&e=1030105c7f), a beloved VA-1 tell-all about our favorite Congressman-in-thief, Rob Wittman (because we all got robbed), recently posted three charts comparing where all VA-1 primary candidates stand on the issues. What sets Ericka Kopp apart from the other candidates? She has “the most expansive progressive platform in the field, including abolishing ICE, releasing the full Epstein files, raising the minimum wage to $30/hour, and impeaching Trump on day one.” One of the eight candidates, Lewis Littlepage, has since withdrawn his campaign. So now there are seven swans a-swimming.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
### Meet and Greet with Ericka
---
| | June 7, 1 PM-4 PM
---
| [Sign Up](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=9b817a1366&e=1030105c7f)
---
| | | [If you believe in Ericka’s grassroots campaign for Congress and in building a future rooted in dignity and opportunity, we invite you to attend our next Meet and Greet from 1 PM to 4 PM on June 7th.](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=db702712c1&e=1030105c7f) Come when you can and leave when you need to, but make sure to register as space is limited.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
### Kitchen Table Talks
---
| | Next talk: May 17,
11 AM-12 PM
---
| [Sign Up](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=edb795f78e&e=1030105c7f)
---
| | | This Sunday, May 17th, from 11 AM - 12 PM, we’re holding another unscripted virtual talk. These are opportunities for you to share what you need to see change in DC for Virginia. Ericka wants to hear about the issues most central to you and your family. Free event; [register](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=a4f6991b23&e=1030105c7f) for the Zoom link.
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |
### This campaign is powered by people.
---
| | Every dollar counts.
---
| [Chip in Today](https://erickakopp.us18.list-manage.com/track/click?u=be2b03077b3c4d3385f5eaa6f&id=ee42931d49&e=1030105c7f)
---
| | | We can’t run this campaign without your help. Every dollar you give goes directly to organizing, knocking on doors, and getting Ericka’s message to voters who are ready for change. We don’t take money from corporations, AIPAC, lobbyists, or billionaires; we rely on individual donations to meet our campaign needs. No matter the amount you invest in Ericka’s campaign, your contribution matters! So if you are tired of being ignored by Washington, chip in now and be part of the movement to fix it.

He is a retired F-18 pilot, and I’m a proud Navy wife and mother to four amazing children. As the granddaughter of a veteran, daughter of a veteran, spouse of a veteran, and mother of future veterans, I come from a PROUD military family.[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNTE1X0VSLU05LjExMDExN190MTkwMDMxMC0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDUxNV9FUi1NOS4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MDAzMTAtMjA2OCJ9/jEbJJ1Y0RyN2G3MSNXS1uQ)I also served in the Navy. That photo above is my helicopter with my call sign on it - “Blossom.” I was winged as a naval aviator in 1995 and served our nation for a total of 10 years as a helicopter pilot flying H-46 and H-3 helicopters, completing two deployments to the Persian Gulf.[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNTE1X0VSLU05LjExMDExN190MTkwMDMxMC0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDUxNV9FUi1NOS4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MDAzMTAtMjA2OCJ9/bVa4HnLiSOWojRb1rwzxgA)After serving in the Navy, I used my GI Bill benefits to go back to school and become a Geriatric Nurse Practitioner. It was an honor to care for our Greatest Generation, and I helped them fight the system to get the healthcare they deserve.
Over time, I got frustrated watching the evening news and just hearing about all the dysfunction and radical agendas in our government. But I’m not one to just complain about problems. I like to solve them.
So I got off my couch, and I ran for office.[](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNTE1X0VSLU05LjExMDExN190MTkwMDMxMC0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDUxNV9FUi1NOS4xMTAxMTdfdDE5MDAzMTAtMjA2OCJ9/gYz1epPzR6QjW2lef8MFYA)I served three sessions in the Virginia State Senate, where I used my real-world experience to actually solve problems. I was proud to champion legislation to promote election security, establish a Military Spouse Liaison, and advocate for patients, families, and caregivers in long-term care facilities.

We were represented by a Democrat who voted with Nancy Pelosi 99% of the time, and I felt we needed a representative who would actually put our values and community first.

I’m leading the charge to lower prices, cut taxes, get better care for our veterans, support military families, and secure the border. We’re making good progress, but all our progress could be in jeopardy if we lose in the upcoming elections.
See, that same Democrat I defeated in 2022 is back for revenge. She just announced her campaign against me, and she raised over $500,000 from Democrat activists in just a few days. Americans deserve transparency.
| | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131466708/621202273/623074613?code=jtk1460-su-nd1&refcode=jtk1460-su-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDRkYjFlOTQtN2Y1MC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xrXDN3NfQCYlRpTTP-ojGK-05NM-Pf5eCJK43TQN7tA=&emci=edae0266-6a50-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=44db1e94-7f50-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=9329426)

Friend,

This week, a reporter asked Donald Trump a simple question: “To what extent are Americans’ financial situations motivating you to make a deal?”
His answer? “ _Not even a little bit._ ”
Gas prices are up 50% since the Iran conflict began, at a national average of over $4.50 a gallon. Inflation is the highest in three years at 3.8% annually. The President even campaigned on lowering costs for working families with an emphasis on those gas prices. But now, letting them eat cake seems to be Trump’s mantra.

At a recent hearing with Pete Hegseth, I also attempted to get answers on behalf of families across the nation. I asked what the escalation in Iran has cost, when it will end, and **what the plan is.**
Hegseth lashed out, blamed Biden, and now refuses to put a cost on the conflict that Pentagon officials estimate is at over $29 billion of your taxpayer dollars. I’ll tell you the most generous thing I can say about his performance was that it verged on incompetence.
Here’s the truth: There is no exit strategy. Trump rejected Iran’s recent proposal to end the conflict and warned the current ceasefire is fragile. Oil prices will continue to rise, especially if tensions escalate. And all of his references to guaranteeing that there will not be a nuclear Iran? Despite the vast and unknown expense in dollars, loss of our munitions readiness, and the lives of our service members, no real progress has been made at all.
This is what a reckless, unprepared, and incompetently waged war looks like.
What makes it worse is the administration asking Americans to accept this economic pain without ever asking Congress or the public for authorization in the first place. Maybe preventing a nuclear-armed Iran is worth enormous sacrifice, but in a democracy that decision belongs to the American people, not one man who launched military action without congressional authorization, a plan, and, by his own admission, consideration for the costs to working families.
[**_So today, I’m asking you to stand with me and sign my petition. Do you approve of Trump and Hegseth’s war in Iran?_**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131466714/621202274/-916130664?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&ask=5&code=jtk1460-su-nd1&refcode=jtk1460-su-nd1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTAvMS8xMDM3OTQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDRkYjFlOTQtN2Y1MC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=xrXDN3NfQCYlRpTTP-ojGK-05NM-Pf5eCJK43TQN7tA=&emci=edae0266-6a50-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=44db1e94-7f50-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=9329426)

Hey folks,
I sat down with **Michigan State Senator Mallory McMorrow** for a conversation that covered three big questions facing the country right now: what it means to have a president who feels completely untethered from reality, how billionaire donors and corporate-backed groups are flooding Democratic primaries with dark money, and why accountability still matters -- from corruption to the Epstein cover-up to the damage this administration keeps inflicting on working people.
This was also our very first in-person Endless Urgency Live in the new studio, and you can feel that energy throughout the conversation. We talked about Trump's overnight posting spirals, why Democrats can't substitute messaging for action, how outside groups are trying to buy this Michigan Senate race, and what it actually looks like to govern in a way that improves people's lives.
**Here 's what we got into:**
* [**00:01:07**] Mallory reacts to Trump's overnight posting spree and what it means when the President of the United States feels detached from reality.
* [**00:12:00**] We dig into the flood of AIPAC-aligned, crypto, and corporate money pouring into Democratic primaries -- and why voters are sick of politicians who chase headlines instead of delivering results.
* [**00:15:26**] Mallory breaks down how Michigan Democrats actually passed universal pre-K, school meals, voting rights protections, abortion rights, and affordable housing after flipping the legislature.
* [**00:24:17**] We talk about the Epstein files, institutional corruption, and why Americans increasingly believe there's one system for the rich and another for everybody else.
* [**00:30:01**] The conversation closes on accountability -- what Democrats must do not only to rebuild the economy and restore trust in government, but to ensure there are real consequences for the abuses and corruption of the Trump era.

This episode is about more than Trump. It's about why people feel abandoned, why institutions are failing, and what it would actually take to restore trust in democracy. If you've been frustrated watching Democrats confuse messaging for action, or wondering why voters keep turning to chaos out of desperation, this conversation gets right to the heart of it.
And if you value honest conversations like this, help me keep building them.

This may be the most important fight right now
For years, the Left thought they had a permanent grip on America's youth.

| | | | [](http://links.conservativesfordjt.com/u/click?_t=05b03ef2209247bcbdad7fd5099cd670&_m=ca65e2f90d9849e693936cf24b72e49b&_e=eKIT312QxpsmhqaALeQGwyHd1xGdct9iceCS6yNSRQtK7ExrPB3_T-9-ZhDkK2xL98AwtXD-kPvEpy_JBp-bhwntFWJVcUdAuSE0E4RUMytMjtwHokvjJcg0FPzv89YrYxQ3f-RKlxe6cdFnejQYsqj84V4VluxLYAR1U-2CzXc2c0KxSNCynWthlOv0Q6SrQbhkrIlWpKzqmL1V2aiRffXheB8z7b6t22VAAYKTwVWcbLSXPuCyhaYxm_eUo9c5zGHxULhG6lU9o-0MeL1PX4szwsX1ZngUUkNrRf_wiHTkt5iEpgvyCPSQGJBtRo0vbKgGI8RmXUka7o5qktXjJHb_Gg90gBoHRycJznZT6nP-kYM1Rs8f6EF4npgXH72W4DCRBP5Vq9UE0yl1X5ck3bt9c12c1XCAoeLW2oKIpROcPDiyn_0wbQn4SYvy_G0hM5q5yvJEpN7NgBB2mY18zaJSxQuqDBZPF2Sd_PyFX8JfrthZABuVJ67tD1bCAZ0qNy5Bnq41Q0tEYwYdK5fRAmFc7rvGYzecaaV9vmxONGiDNxUF-GrXEbzAKSZLtJh9UGW4ewERYt7b3lo8dsclIBi2VsGR0wmdZBxY3DZGNLE5WS0We08ccYjqQuuKiO-CieTx7tNuJJIRAjIzDC7xyuvUciuQ9dC-X66VCxDvYt92uW0yB98vG8IsAiC1pHNz)
---
| | | Friend,
---
For years, the Left thought they had a permanent grip on America's youth.

And honestly?

For a while, they did.
They dominated classrooms. Social media. Pop culture. Hollywood. Universities.

They told an entire generation that loving your country was shameful...

That faith was outdated... And traditional values were something to erase.

But thanks to Charlie's leadership, something incredible has happened:

Young men are rejecting the Left in RECORD numbers. High school boys are the most Conservative they've been in 50 years.

And Gen Z is heading back to church -- in numbers greater than their parents' or grandparents' generations.

For the first time in decades, we are WINNING the American Culture War.

**But there 's still one group the Left is desperately fighting to hold onto: **

_America 's young women. _

Because they know something very important, Friend...

If they can win the hearts and minds of young women...

They don't just shape individuals. They shape families. They shape homes. They shape future generations.

It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. clean_body: | | | | Patriot, It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250th birthday. Patriot, this Memorial Day marks the first major national act of remembrance of the veterans who made the ultimate sacrifice to defend America from its enemies and ensure it has remained the Land of the Free for the last 250 years. And this year's National Memorial Day Parade will be a special edition - the biggest parade yet - where national memory meets living history as veterans from every military generation celebrate America and honor the service and sacrifice of their fallen brethren. Patriot, the National Memorial Day Parade is ENIRELY FUNDED by private contributions, including from generous patriots like you. WWII veterans were a key part of the first parade when it was revived in 2005, as they have been every year since for the last 20 years. But this may be the last year we have the opportunity to have these brave men and women with us for the parade. | | | | | | | | This year is a rare moment when living witnesses to World War II and America 's 250th birthday overlap. And no matter how much you can give to this important cause, I want to ask something additional of you. On Memorial Day - not just this momentous year of military milestones, but every year - please join me in honoring those who made the ultimate sacrifice for our freedoms. Come to the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. Visit a local veterans' cemetery. Send a note to a family of the fallen. Or simply take a quiet moment to think about the men and women who gave their lives to defend OUR country. I believe that while we can never do enough to express our gratitude to our defenders, veterans, and first responders, we can always do a little more. Patriot, thank you for your support of America 's heroes. Peter,

**What happens when reliably red states start slipping away?**

We’ve seen it before, the other way around: **In 2016, Trump flipped Michigan and Wisconsin. In 2024, he took Nevada for the first time in two decades.**

Democrats didn’t have a contingency plan, and they paid for it.

But, what if the script flips and puts Republicans in the hot seat?

Recent polls show **Texas, Mississippi, Alaska, Georgia, and North Carolina — long-time Republican strongholds** — are all at serious risk of flipping or becoming highly competitive this November.

**If we lose even one or two of these firewall states, Republicans cannot afford to lose a single additional seat.

That’s why I’m asking you to support my race in Minnesota** — a race that could quietly become one of the most important insurance policies for keeping the Senate majority.

**Even the Goats Know.** Somewhere between fighting for working families and taking on bought and paid for politicians, you end up making a few goat friends too.
That is not a complaint.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/dc24f0b2-108b-4407-9b52-0ad01f880797?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
One of the things I love most about this campaign is that it takes you everywhere. Rural farms at golden hour. Nashville classrooms. Union halls. Front porches. Diners where the coffee is strong and the opinions are stronger. **This district is not one thing and it has never been one thing, and any candidate who thinks they can represent it from a distance has already lost the plot.**_**[Help me get to Congress, and set the record straight: every corner of our districts deserve representation!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ee4a8de9-ab3b-4dc7-a7f9-0fadd826f713?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
[ DONATE $15 TODAY!!️](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ee4a8de9-ab3b-4dc7-a7f9-0fadd826f713?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Tennessee is working families stretching a paycheck. It is students learning a trade. It is farmers who were here before the subdivisions and will be here long after the headlines move on. It is communities that have been carved up, talked over, and told to wait their turn.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7146d5e7-8dfa-4ce5-be98-3deaf1ae015e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I am not interested in a campaign that lives in a conference room. I want to be where you are. Even if where you are involves two baby goats and a makeshift fence.
But here is the thing. I didn't come from money, power, or have the right last name. My wife and I both grew up around abuse, addiction, and crime. We know what it means to fight your way out and build your way up with nothing but grit and the stubborn belief that things can be different.
**[If you want that kind of fighter in Congress, help us build this campaign today.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ee4a8de9-ab3b-4dc7-a7f9-0fadd826f713?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Help our fight today.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ee4a8de9-ab3b-4dc7-a7f9-0fadd826f713?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I built a career from the ground up in the music industry, eventually working on Grammy nominated albums and sold out world tours. Twenty five years later, Nashville is home. These communities are home, and I have watched long enough as Big Money in politics and bad leadership have pushed working families to the sidelines while the people in power protect their own seats, their own paychecks, and their invitations to the right fundraisers.
**That is why I am running for Congress.** Somebody has to, and I would rather lose telling the truth than win by crawling. This is what Hometowns Over Headlines actually looks like: a candidate who shows up, gets his hands dirty, and never forgets who he is fighting for. _Even the hoofed ones._

body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

Right now, Utah is at the center of a raging storm after the local
government green-lit one of the world’s largest data centers over the
furious objections of thousands of local residents.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38288?source=email-20260515&t=1011&akid=10738%2E5885482%2EnZaAhR ]Headline: 'Irresponsible': backlash as Utah approves datacenter twice
the size of Manhattan.

This behemoth project – backed by Shark Tank venture capitalist Kevin
O’Leary, known as “Mr. Wonderful” – will span more than twice the size of
Manhattan, guzzling up enough water and power to imperil the Great Salt
Lake and threaten drinking water for nearby communities.

It’s not just Utah. Community after community – red states and blue – are
fighting back against mega data centers that send utility bills soaring
and drain precious water from already stressed rivers and lakes. And
Bernie is again showing what leadership looks like, demanding Congress
pass a nationwide moratorium on new mega data centers.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38288?source=email-20260515&t=1012&akid=10738%2E5885482%2EnZaAhR ]Right now, Our Revolution is fighting back at both the local level and
the national level — and we need you with us. Will you stand with Bernie
and demand an urgent moratorium on giant new data centers, NOW?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38288?source=email-20260515&t=1013&akid=10738%2E5885482%2EnZaAhR ]ADD YOUR NAME

We know what happens when data centers move in: 24-hour noise, water
shortages, and sharp hikes to our power bills – on top of Trump’s energy
price hikes. This is about ultra-wealthy investors destroying our
communities for their own profits, while our neighborhoods, environment,
and wallets pay the price.

Nobody wants these gigantic data centers – and one community after the
next is saying NO. Through local grassroots pushback, a small city in
Wisconsin was able to pass the nation’s first-ever anti-data center
referendum by a 2-to-1 landslide, despite pro-corporate propaganda
covering the airwaves.

It’s time for a people-powered national revolt. Which is why Our
Revolution is recruiting our 100,000-strong Citizen Action Team to bring
relentless outside pressure: calling, organizing, and showing up to stand
up for community needs. And while we organize locally, we ALSO need to be
backing Bernie’s call for a pause on the construction of new facilities
until Congress passes regulations to protect our communities.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38288?source=email-20260515&t=1014&akid=10738%2E5885482%2EnZaAhR ]Headline: A movement to ban data centers gains steam across the U.S.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38288?source=email-20260515&t=1015&akid=10738%2E5885482%2EnZaAhR ]Momentum is building across the country, and now is the time to double
down. Will you send an urgent message to your member of Congress to demand
a halt to reckless data center expansion?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/38288?source=email-20260515&t=1016&akid=10738%2E5885482%2EnZaAhR ]ADD YOUR NAME

Big Tech billionaires and Wall Street sharks want us to sit quietly while
they raid our resources – even as communities across the country are
standing up to say “NO.” We need you in this fight. Because if we don’t
act, no town is safe from becoming the next data center sacrifice zone.

When we organize, we win,

Our Revolution

This election for Democrats isn't a need to win. It's an absolute have to win.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131469237/621210986/57398372?refcode=em26_260515_MSNow_fnd_gq_act___AB_ettx&utm_campaign=em26_260515_MSNow_fnd_gq_act___AB_ettx&utm_medium=email&refcode2=df10f9c9-8350-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZGYxMGY5YzktODM1MC1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=B1s3ubccrPW1E1QRk1SXtv6AbfPp7u-i629CmTx__EQ=) Peter,

Last week, I sat down with Ali Vitali at MS NOW and said something I want to say to you directly:

This election for Democrats isn't a need-to-win. It's an absolute _have_ -to-win.

I meant every word of it.

We have 36 governor's races on the ballot this November. Thirty-six. And I believe that we can win in places people have written off. Iowa. Ohio. States that have drifted red but where the collision of Trump's tariffs, rising prices, and a healthcare system that's being hollowed out has people looking for something different.

Because here's what I've learned from winning three times in a state that went for Donald Trump by 30 points: people don't vote for a party. They vote for someone they trust to make their life better. Someone who can tell them not just what they're going to do, but why – what actually drives them to do this work.

Voters are craving authenticity right now. They want results and they want receipts.

And Democratic governors deliver. We create good jobs. We expand healthcare. We keep our promises. And right now, we are the most important line of defense against an administration that has absolutely no solutions for the families who are stretched thin at the end of every month.

When I talked about Ohio's Amy Acton and Iowa's Rob Sand, I wasn't just talking about two candidates. I was talking about what it looks like when we go on offense. When we compete everywhere. When we refuse to concede any state and any voter before the campaign even starts.

If we win those governor's mansions in Iowa and Ohio, we don't just help the people of those states. We build a map for the future that doesn't depend on five states and zero margin of error.

But none of this happens without resources.

## The Capitalist exists because of you, and we want to hear from you!
**[Become a paid subscriber today to support The Capitalist
and access the Live Capitalist chat](https://substack.com/redirect/e84a42e3-0482-450f-8835-936dcb149638?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Subscribe here now](https://substack.com/redirect/e84a42e3-0482-450f-8835-936dcb149638?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
China just agreed to buy 200 Boeing jets. Not a press release full of vague promises. Not some future framework. A straight-up order, announced by President Trump after sitting down with Xi Jinping in Beijing this week. That's the kind of concrete number that actually moves the needle for American factories, suppliers, and paychecks.
Boeing's own CEO, Kelly Ortberg, had called the potential "a big number" but tied it explicitly to whatever Trump and Xi could hammer out. Trump pushed and got 200--more than Boeing had initially pitched at 150. These are mostly 737 Max narrowbodies, the workhorse planes Chinese airlines desperately need after years of leaning on Airbus instead. Boeing hadn't landed a major order from China in nearly a decade.
What makes this more than just another aircraft sale is how it happened. Trump didn't roll into Beijing with a handful of diplomats and lobbyists. He brought the deepest bench of American corporate firepower assembled in decades: Boeing's Ortberg, Tesla and SpaceX's Elon Musk, Apple's Tim Cook, Nvidia's Jensen Huang, BlackRock's Larry Fink, Citigroup's Jane Fraser, Cargill's Brian Sikes, and others from Qualcomm, Exxon, Blackstone, Mastercard and Visa. These aren't symbolic names. They run companies that employ hundreds of thousands, move trillions, and sit at the sharp end of both manufacturing and cutting-edge tech and finance. The message was unmistakable: America's business leadership was at the table, not watching from the sidelines.
This wasn't some feel-good photo op. It was deal-making with leverage. Despite all the tariff friction, the threats, the supply-chain arguments, and the endless Washington hand-wringing about "decoupling," the simple fact remains: China still needs what America builds. Commercial jets that fly reliably and efficiently. Advanced AI chips that power the next generation of computing. Boeing planes fill airline fleets. Nvidia silicon keeps data centers humming. Beijing can talk tough about self-reliance all it wants, but the math on the ground says otherwise. The two biggest economies on the planet still need each other in ways that sanctions and speeches and even spats over tariffs can't erase.

The lowest denomination of our currency is being wiped out by the same force that is silently, steadily, and relentlessly eating away at your hard-earned savings, 401(k), and purchasing power.
You need to understand the mechanics of this major threat--**and how you could help protect yourself** --now, before the next wave of inflation potentially hits.
Your Defensive Strategy Starts Here ( and it's FREE)
[Click here NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/611273ca-3af7-4b18-8194-523ee18cdefc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
The Boeing order alone is a direct win for American industry. Boeing's commercial airplane business has been grinding through production ramps, quality issues, and a post-pandemic recovery that's been anything but smooth. A fresh 200-plane commitment from China's state-backed carriers means steady work for factories in Washington state, South Carolina, and the thousands of suppliers scattered across the country. These aren't abstract "good for GDP" numbers. They translate into welders, engineers, machinists, and logistics workers who get overtime, benefits, and job security. Aviation is one of the few sectors where the U.S. still holds a clear global edge. Keeping those order books full matters more than any tariff tweet ever could.
Xi didn't stop at the aircraft deal. He told the assembled CEOs, point blank, that China's door to U.S. business will "open wider." State media quoted him saying American companies have benefited from China's reforms and that U.S. firms will enjoy "even broader prospects" going forward. That's not boilerplate. It came directly to Musk, Cook, Huang, and the rest while Trump sat there. Xi knows the delegation represented real money and real technology. He also knows China's economy is under pressure--slowing growth, property troubles, demographic headwinds. Opening wider isn't charity; it's pragmatism. The CEOs heard it loud and clear.
None of this erases the bigger trade fights. Tariffs are still in place. Tech export controls still exist. Supply-chain security remains a legitimate worry for both sides. But the Beijing summit cut through the noise and showed what actually gets results: high-level, personal deal-making backed by the people who run the companies that matter. Trump has always sold himself as the guy who can sit across from tough negotiators and extract concessions. This week he delivered something measurable. Two hundred planes. A signal of wider market access. And a reminder that, for all the rhetoric, America still holds cards China wants to play.
* * *
* * *

[ Have a view? Let us know!](https://substack.com/redirect/ea7616d1-f218-4a1b-b35a-6f49b25a1077?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
The president's critics will downplay it. They'll call it transactional, short-term, or somehow beneath the dignity of grand strategy. Fine. Grand strategy is what you talk about when you're not closing deals. The workers who build 737s in Everett, Washington, don't get paid in theories. They get paid when orders land. The suppliers who machine parts for those planes don't care about ideological purity tests; they care about the next purchase order. This deal puts cash in their pockets and steel in the supply chain.
It also undercuts the narrative that America has nothing left to offer except lectures. China's airlines need planes now. Its tech sector needs chips it can't yet replicate at scale. Xi's "open wider" line was a public acknowledgment that U.S. companies remain essential partners, not just rivals to be squeezed out. That's leverage worth using. Not forever, not without guardrails, but right now, while the numbers still favor us.
No one should pretend this resets the entire U.S.-China relationship. One aircraft order and some warm words from Xi don't solve intellectual-property theft, forced technology transfer, or the military tensions in the South China Sea. But dismissing concrete economic wins because **they don 't solve every problem** is how you end up with no wins at all. Trump showed up with the CEOs who actually run things. He got a deal on jets. He got China talking about broader access. And he reminded everyone that when the world's two largest economies sit down, the conversation still starts with what each side can buy and sell.
That's not flashy. It's not revolutionary. It's just business--the kind that keeps American factories running and American workers employed. In a town full of people who prefer endless strategic seminars, this week's results in Beijing were refreshingly straightforward: America had what China needed, Trump brought the team that could deliver it, and the order book moved.
For once, the deal actually happened.

You need to understand the mechanics of this major threat--and how you could help protect yourself --now, before the next wave of inflation potentially hits. Your Defensive Strategy Starts Here ( and it's FREE) The Boeing order alone is a direct win for American industry. Boeing's commercial airplane business has been grinding through production ramps, quality issues, and a post-pandemic recovery that's been anything but smooth. A fresh 200-plane commitment from China's state-backed carriers means steady work for factories in Washington state, South Carolina, and the thousands of suppliers scattered across the country. These aren't abstract "good for GDP" numbers. They translate into welders, engineers, machinists, and logistics workers who get overtime, benefits, and job security. Aviation is one of the few sectors where the U.S. still holds a clear global edge. Keeping those order books full matters more than any tariff tweet ever could. Xi didn't stop at the aircraft deal. He told the assembled CEOs, point blank, that China's door to U.S. business will "open wider." State media quoted him saying American companies have benefited from China's reforms and that U.S. firms will enjoy "even broader prospects" going forward. That's not boilerplate. It came directly to Musk, Cook, Huang, and the rest while Trump sat there. Xi knows the delegation represented real money and real technology. He also knows China's economy is under pressure--slowing growth, property troubles, demographic headwinds. Opening wider isn't charity; it's pragmatism. The CEOs heard it loud and clear. None of this erases the bigger trade fights. Tariffs are still in place. Tech export controls still exist. Supply-chain security remains a legitimate worry for both sides. But the Beijing summit cut through the noise and showed what actually gets results: high-level, personal deal-making backed by the people who run the companies that matter. Trump has always sold himself as the guy who can sit across from tough negotiators and extract concessions. This week he delivered something measurable. Two hundred planes. A signal of wider market access. And a reminder that, for all the rhetoric, America still holds cards China wants to play. The president's critics will downplay it. They'll call it transactional, short-term, or somehow beneath the dignity of grand strategy. Fine. Grand strategy is what you talk about when you're not closing deals. The workers who build 737s in Everett, Washington, don't get paid in theories. They get paid when orders land. The suppliers who machine parts for those planes don't care about ideological purity tests; they care about the next purchase order. This deal puts cash in their pockets and steel in the supply chain. It also undercuts the narrative that America has nothing left to offer except lectures. China's airlines need planes now. Its tech sector needs chips it can't yet replicate at scale. Xi's "open wider" line was a public acknowledgment that U.S. companies remain essential partners, not just rivals to be squeezed out. That's leverage worth using. Not forever, not without guardrails, but right now, while the numbers still favor us. No one should pretend this resets the entire U.S.-China relationship. One aircraft order and some warm words from Xi don't solve intellectual-property theft, forced technology transfer, or the military tensions in the South China Sea. But dismissing concrete economic wins because they don 't solve every problem is how you end up with no wins at all. Trump showed up with the CEOs who actually run things. He got a deal on jets. He got China talking about broader access. And he reminded everyone that when the world's two largest economies sit down, the conversation still starts with what each side can buy and sell. That's not flashy. It's not revolutionary. It's just business--the kind that keeps American factories running and American workers employed. In a town full of people who prefer endless strategic seminars, this week's results in Beijing were refreshingly straightforward: America had what China needed, Trump brought the team that could deliver it, and the order book moved. For once, the deal actually happened. subject: Katie doesn’t flinch:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Governor 2026
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41351%2E3422442%2E0f4-Ep)
Peter, it’s Elizabeth Warren.
We need leaders who aren’t afraid to walk into a room with rich and powerful Wall Street bankers or stand toe-to-toe with Donald Trump and still come out on top, fighting for working people.
And that’s exactly why I’m supporting Katie Porter for Governor of California.
I’ve spent my career taking on the biggest corporations and the richest executives in this country. I know what it takes to win those fights—and I know how rare it is to find someone who doesn’t flinch when the pressure comes.
**Katie Porter doesn’t flinch.**
She’s tough. She’s fearless. And she understands something some politicians forget the minute they get comfortable in office: Government is supposed to work for working people, not for billionaires and corporate donors.
California’s June primary election is just weeks away. And right now, corporate PACs and wealthy special interests are flooding this race with money because they know what Katie represents: _real accountability and real change._
Katie’s the only candidate in this race who has always refused corporate money, and she’s fighting for things that actually matter to people’s lives: universal childcare, Medicare for All, and affordable housing.
When voters hear what she’s fighting for, they respond. But only if her message reaches them—before the ads, the special interests, and the big money try to drown it out.
Katie is being outspent, so I’m asking you directly:
**[Can you chip in $5 today to help power Katie Porter’s campaign and make sure Californians hear her message?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260515_1_ak.uXNcCK&refcode=em20260515-41351&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=3&akid=41351%2E3422442%2E0f4-Ep)**

Elizabeth

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Demand Justice PAC
body:
I’ve spent enough time in politics to know this: when Democrats stop
showing up in certain places, somebody else fills the void.

Usually, it’s people who have no real interest in helping working families
— just dividing them, distracting them, and cashing in while communities
get left behind. After a while, that kind of politics takes a toll. People
start feeling like nobody sees them, nobody hears them, and nobody is
fighting for the places they call home.

I think there’s a better path.

It starts by taking small towns seriously. It starts by respecting people
enough to tell the truth. And it starts by showing up, organizing, and
competing in places too many folks in politics have given up on. That’s a
big part of why I’m launching Small Town PAC.

Small Town PAC is about helping Democrats expand the map by building power
in small towns and backing the kind of politics that actually speak to
working families. Because if we want to win in more places, we’ve got to
be willing to show up in more places.

That’s the work ahead, and I’m asking you to be part of it from the start.

Peter,

In the Democratic primary for Pennsylvania’s 3rd Congressional district,
Justice Democrats-endorsed progressive Chris Rabb is surging against two
establishment opponents. But Democratic leadership is swooping in at the
last minute to stop his momentum.

First, it was looking like Ala Stanford was our biggest opponent, but her
campaign nosedived after reports about her ties to AIPAC surfaced. Her

May 15, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**Turning Point Action Endorses Trump-Endorsed Conservative Julia Letlow for U.S. Senate** _National conservative grassroots organization backs Letlow as the strongest America First candidate in Louisiana Senate race_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — Turning Point Action has announced its endorsement of Congresswoman Julia Letlow, the Trump-endorsed candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, citing her strong conservative record, support for President Trump’s America First agenda, and commitment to fighting for Louisiana families.
_“I am honored to earn the endorsement of Turning Point Action,”_**said Congresswoman Julia Letlow.** _“Turning Point Action has been on the frontlines of the conservative movement, mobilizing grassroots patriots across the country to defend our values and fight for the future of America. I’m proud to stand alongside President Trump and organizations like Turning Point Action as we work to keep the border secure, unleash American energy, and protect our children.”_
---
|
---
| | Turning Point Action joins a growing coalition of conservatives rallying behind Letlow’s campaign, which continues to build momentum across Louisiana ahead of the May 16 Republican primary.
As a member of Congress, Letlow has built a strong conservative record fighting for Louisiana families, authoring the Parents’ Bill of Rights, standing with law enforcement, supporting Louisiana energy producers and farmers, and backing President Trump’s agenda in Congress.
Congresswoman Julia Letlow is the Trump-endorsed candidate for U.S. Senate in Louisiana, a mother of two, educator, and conservative fighter who has represented Louisiana’s Fifth Congressional District since 2021.

Peter,

I wanted to personally reach out one last time before our mid-month fundraising deadline tonight at midnight.

This Sunday, we're opening our new campaign office, and I've been thinking a lot about what that really means. To me, it's not just a building or a place to put campaign signs. _It's a sign of what we're building together_ — a campaign rooted in community, in showing up, and in staying connected to the people I serve.

The best work happens when you stay close to the community, when you listen more than you talk, and when people know they can walk through the door, ask questions, share concerns, and feel heard. That's what I want this office to be. But, as always, I'm going to be blunt: opening a new office means investing in this work in a bigger way.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | The ink is already dry on Executive Order 14028. | Most Americans ignored it because it sounds like a boring bureaucracy. * * *
Dear Friend, My name is Kimberly Bretches. I'm a wife and a mother of four young children. And I'm writing to you today because I am out of options and I am terrified. I'll be honest, asking strangers for help doesn't come naturally to me. But neither does the idea of my husband spending the rest of his life in prison for doing his job — so here I am. Chance is a police officer in Austin, Texas. He is, without question, the best man I know. He has spent his career keeping dangerous people off the streets, protecting a city that doesn't always make it easy to do so, and coming home every night to a family that needs him. His supervisors have praised him for his professionalism, for his instincts, for his dedication. He is exactly the kind of officer you want showing up when things go wrong. | By every measure, Chance did everything right. He used department-approved tools, following his training, to protect his fellow officers and the people of Austin.
---
And in May of 2020, things went very wrong in Austin. For three consecutive days, our city was under siege. Violent agitators hurled rocks, frozen water bottles, and exploding fireworks directly at police officers. Buildings were vandalized and looted. Police vehicles were set on fire. A rioter was caught with a Molotov cocktail. Officers were injured. The city was teetering on the edge of complete chaos, and everyone knew it.
On May 31st, the third day, when the mob was larger and more dangerous than it had ever been, Chance was on the front lines. He did what he was trained to do. He deployed non-lethal, department-approved beanbag projectiles to stop the aggression and protect his fellow officers and the people of Austin. The crowd eventually dispersed. The city held.
**No one questioned what he did that night. His supervisors praised his response. His department stood behind him.**
And then Austin elected District Attorney José Garza.
Instead of holding the rioters accountable — the ones who threw the fireworks, who lit the fires, who carried the Molotov cocktails — Garza turned his attention to the officers who stopped them. He launched an indiscriminate campaign against law enforcement, using the power of his office not to protect the public, but to make political examples out of good cops.
Chance became one of his targets.
| Chance now faces up to 99 Years in prison — for following his training.
---
My husband now faces up to 99 years in prison. Not because he did anything wrong. Not because his department found fault with his actions. Not because any credible review of that night concluded he acted improperly. But because one politically-motivated prosecutor decided the officers who held the line deserved to be punished for holding it. This case has been grinding through the system for years now. The trial has already been delayed several times and is **now scheduled for June of this year.** Every continuance, every filing, every hearing means more hours of legal work, and more bills our family has to find a way to pay. I am asking for your help because we cannot do this alone. The National Center for Police Defense has been in Chance's corner, and your donation goes toward funding his legal defense, ensuring he has the representation he deserves as he walks into that courtroom in June.

clean_body: | Officer Chance Bretches and his family — Austin, Texas Dear Friend, My name is Kimberly Bretches. I'm a wife and a mother of four young children. And I'm writing to you today because I am out of options and I am terrified. I'll be honest, asking strangers for help doesn't come naturally to me. But neither does the idea of my husband spending the rest of his life in prison for doing his job — so here I am. Chance is a police officer in Austin, Texas. He is, without question, the best man I know. He has spent his career keeping dangerous people off the streets, protecting a city that doesn't always make it easy to do so, and coming home every night to a family that needs him. His supervisors have praised him for his professionalism, for his instincts, for his dedication. He is exactly the kind of officer you want showing up when things go wrong. | By every measure, Chance did everything right. He used department-approved tools, following his training, to protect his fellow officers and the people of Austin. And in May of 2020, things went very wrong in Austin. For three consecutive days, our city was under siege. Violent agitators hurled rocks, frozen water bottles, and exploding fireworks directly at police officers. Buildings were vandalized and looted. Police vehicles were set on fire. A rioter was caught with a Molotov cocktail. Officers were injured. The city was teetering on the edge of complete chaos, and everyone knew it. On May 31st, the third day, when the mob was larger and more dangerous than it had ever been, Chance was on the front lines. He did what he was trained to do. He deployed non-lethal, department-approved beanbag projectiles to stop the aggression and protect his fellow officers and the people of Austin. The crowd eventually dispersed. The city held. No one questioned what he did that night. His supervisors praised his response. His department stood behind him. And then Austin elected District Attorney José Garza. Instead of holding the rioters accountable — the ones who threw the fireworks, who lit the fires, who carried the Molotov cocktails — Garza turned his attention to the officers who stopped them. He launched an indiscriminate campaign against law enforcement, using the power of his office not to protect the public, but to make political examples out of good cops. Chance became one of his targets. | Chance now faces up to 99 Years in prison — for following his training. My husband now faces up to 99 years in prison. Not because he did anything wrong. Not because his department found fault with his actions. Not because any credible review of that night concluded he acted improperly. But because one politically-motivated prosecutor decided the officers who held the line deserved to be punished for holding it. This case has been grinding through the system for years now. The trial has already been delayed several times and is now scheduled for June of this year. Every continuance, every filing, every hearing means more hours of legal work, and more bills our family has to find a way to pay. I am asking for your help because we cannot do this alone. The National Center for Police Defense has been in Chance's corner, and your donation goes toward funding his legal defense, ensuring he has the representation he deserves as he walks into that courtroom in June. | · · · or any amount you can give If you believe that the men and women who run toward danger deserve better than this, . Fellow Conservative,
_
**What happens when reliably red states start slipping away?**

We’ve seen it before, the other way around: **In 2016, Trump flipped Michigan and Wisconsin. In 2024, he took Nevada for the first time in two decades.**

Democrats didn’t have a contingency plan, and they paid for it.

But, what if the script flips and puts Republicans in the hot seat?

Recent polls show **Texas, Mississippi, Alaska, Georgia, and North Carolina — long-time Republican strongholds** — are all at serious risk of flipping or becoming highly competitive this November.

**If we lose even one or two of these firewall states, Republicans cannot afford to lose a single additional seat.

That’s why I’m asking you to support my race in Minnesota** — a race that could quietly become one of the most important insurance policies for keeping the Senate majority.

As a former Navy SEAL, I don’t believe in hoping for the best. **I prepare for the worst and fight to win.** With your help, we can flip this seat, double the number of SEALs in the U.S. Senate, and give our party critical reinforcements no matter what happens in the South or the Far North.
