Katie Britt (R., Ala.) is once again at the center of one of the Trump administration’s biggest family policy rollouts, and at the heart of her new effort is TrumpRx, the direct-to-consumer drug pricing platform that Republicans have made the cornerstone of their affordability agenda. Britt joined President Donald Trump in the Oval Office on Monday to launch Moms.gov, a new Department of Health and Human Services site that went live on Mother’s Day. The site is a clearinghouse of resources for expecting and new mothers, covering nutrition, breastfeeding, mental health, adoption, and the administration’s new “Trump Accounts” savings program for newborns. Republicans are going to disenfranchise every Democrat in the state
#

Peter, we should all be paying attention to what’s happening in South Carolina.
The Republican governor is taking his marching orders from Trump and called a special session on redistricting. The plan is simple, and predictable:
They’re going to draw a racist map that silences Black voters and eliminates Congressman Jim Clyburn’s seat — the only Democratic district in the entire state.
[**We can’t let this happen, and the fight isn’t over. Split a donation now between Congressman Clyburn’s campaign and mine to join the fight.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-clyburn.rhMXVW&refcode=em260515-2-160&t=1&akid=4136%2E734936%2EKlOlWz)

Voto Latino is organizing right now, not later, to let voters know what’s at stake this November.
#
Peter,
In 2024, Trump and Republicans campaigned on lowering costs. Many Latino voters heard that message and hoped for relief.
**Instead, it’s working families that are still getting hit from every direction. Their rent is still too high, groceries cost way too much, and many are risking their health by opting out of health insurance just to cover other costs at home.**
And while families do the math at the kitchen table, Trump and Congressional Republicans are pushing policies that make it worse, not easier, on families.
**That’s why Voto Latino is organizing right now, not later, to let voters know what’s at stake this November.** If we don’t show up in mass numbers to vote in November, there’s a high probability that our economy is going to continue dragging in the coming years.
**[If you want to help power Voto Latino’s voter registration and mobilization efforts in key states, will you pitch in $3 right now?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260515-2-ak.bYZQd2&amount=3&refcode=em20260515-134&t=1&akid=134%2E1366028%2EYSQSaX)**
We’re registering and mobilizing Latino voters in key states, sharing trusted voting information, and fighting back against disinformation designed to confuse people or discourage them from participating.
Because this fall, Latino voters can help decide the outcome of the midterm elections. _But only if we prepare now._
**We set a goal to raise $10,000 by midnight tomorrow** so we can keep organizing, keep reaching voters, and keep expanding our voter registration and outreach work where it matters most.

subject: Announcing: James Talarico, Ruwa Romman, and more!

body:
Way to Lead PAC [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA015/1/91128/images/Logo-White-BG.png]
Peter,

Big news—we're excited to officially throw our support behind eight new candidates in five states !

We didn't make these decisions lightly. After digging into each race, talking with folks on the ground, and looking closely at where each candidate stands, it became clear that our endorsees are the real deal. Each of them gets what's at stake in 2026 and has been a strong voice on the issues that matter deeply to our community, to working people, and to our mission at Way to Lead.

https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
James Talarico, Texas
U.S. Senate (General Election, Flip)
—
James Talarico is an eighth-generation Texan, former middle school teacher, and Presbyterian seminarian who has served in the Texas House of Representatives since 2018. As a state representative, James has led the fight against the billionaire mega-donors and puppet politicians who have taken over Texas. He passed bipartisan legislation to fund public schools, expand job opportunities for young adults, and lower the cost of child care, housing, and prescription drugs. Now, he's running for U.S. Senate to take his fight against corruption to Washington and win power back for working people.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
JoAnna Mendoza, Arizona
Congressional District 6 (General Election, Flip)
—
Raised in a farmworker family in Pinal County, JoAnna experienced firsthand the realities of rural poverty and the power of community. At just 17, Jo answered the call to serve, enlisting in the U.S. Navy before joining the U.S. Marine Corps, where she deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan and trained the next generation of Marines as a Drill Instructor. After 20 years of service, Jo returned home to raise her son and continue her life of service. In the Marines, Jo stood on the frontlines for our country; in Congress, she will fight for Southern Arizona by working to lower costs and create economic opportunity.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
Clara Pratte, Arizona
Corporation Commission (General Election, Flip)
—
As a member of the Navajo Nation, Clara Pratte grew up in Lupton, Arizona, without electricity or running water until middle school. Now a business owner and co-founder of Navajo Power, Clara promotes responsible solar development across the Southwest, and, if elected, would become the first Native American to win statewide office in Arizona history. She is running for Arizona's Corporation Commission to lower costs, protect consumers, and make Arizona a better, more affordable state for all.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
Miracle Rankin, Georgia
State Supreme Court (General Election (May), Flip)
—
As a trial attorney representing individuals who have suffered a catastrophic injury, Miracle Rankin built her career taking on the most powerful interests and winning. Miracle is running for the Supreme Court of Georgia to ensure that the State's highest court remains a place where the courtroom remains open and accessible to everyday citizens, and where the Constitution protects the people, not just the powerful.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
Jen Jordan, Georgia
State Supreme Court (General Election (May), Flip)
—
Jen Jordan has spent 25 years as an attorney and then as a state senator fighting for everyday Georgians. Raised in Dodge County by a single mother who worked as a hairdresser, she learned the value of hard work and perseverance early. Throughout her career, Jen has worked to protect voting and privacy rights, hold corporate polluters accountable, and defend children from abuse. Jen is running because she knows that Georgians need a Supreme Court that will stand up and protect everyone's rights.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
Ruwa Romman, Georgia
SD-07 (Primary Election)
—
State Representative Ruwa Romman is the first Palestinian elected to any public office in the state of Georgia. While some know Representative Romman as the Palestinian speaker who wasn't allowed onstage at the 2024 DNC, she has also been organizing in Georgia for over 12 years to flip the state. Ruwa is now running for State Senate because the old playbook has failed too many times. At a moment of fear and uncertainty, Ruwa believes that when we all organize, we can build a better future.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
Brenda Zamora, Nevada
Clark County School District Board of Trustees
District D (General Election, Protect)
—
Brenda Zamora is an immigrant daughter and mother of three who knows firsthand the challenges families face in education. Brenda's involvement in education advocacy began when her eldest daughter faced challenges early on, becoming her catalyst for community engagement. With four years on the Clark County school board, she has worked tirelessly to bridge the gap between families and schools, ensuring every voice is heard. She is deeply committed to protecting all our marginalized communities and making sure all families have a meaningful seat at the table.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]
Winn Decker, North Carolina
HD-37 (General Election, Flip)
—
Winn Decker is a Democrat running to flip North Carolina House District 37 in southern Wake County, one of the most competitive seats in the state. The son of two public school teachers from rural Tennessee, Winn came to North Carolina over a decade ago to earn his Ph.D. in Public Administration from NC State and put down roots in Fuquay-Varina. At the Hunt Institute, founded by former four-term Governor Jim Hunt, he worked across party lines with governors and legislators to strengthen public schools, expand access to higher education, and build a workforce ready for a changing economy. He coaches youth basketball and volunteers in the community he is fighting to represent. Winn's campaign is built around the pressures southern Wake families face every day: rising housing costs, unaffordable childcare, overcrowded schools, and a cost of living that keeps outpacing wages. He believes government can work for the people and is ready to prove it.

So what does this mean? We're all in. At Way to Lead PAC, we're laser-focused on winning tight races, where your money and our strategy can make the biggest difference. Our team will be working hard to spread the word, mobilize supporters, and help build the momentum needed to win.

If you're as excited as we are, we'd love for you to join us—whether that's volunteering, donating, or just helping get the word out.

If you're with us, will you make a donation to help elect working-class champions? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/wtl-em-may26]

At just 17, Jo answered the call to serve, enlisting in the U.S. Navy before joining the U.S. Marine Corps, where she deployed to Iraq and Afghanistan and trained the next generation of Marines as a Drill Instructor. After 20 years of service, Jo returned home to raise her son and continue her life of service. In the Marines, Jo stood on the frontlines for our country; in Congress, she will fight for Southern Arizona by working to lower costs and create economic opportunity. [] Clara Pratte, Arizona Corporation Commission (General Election, Flip) — As a member of the Navajo Nation, Clara Pratte grew up in Lupton, Arizona, without electricity or running water until middle school. Now a business owner and co-founder of Navajo Power, Clara promotes responsible solar development across the Southwest, and, if elected, would become the first Native American to win statewide office in Arizona history. She is running for Arizona's Corporation Commission to lower costs, protect consumers, and make Arizona a better, more affordable state for all. [] Miracle Rankin, Georgia State Supreme Court (General Election (May), Flip) — As a trial attorney representing individuals who have suffered a catastrophic injury, Miracle Rankin built her career taking on the most powerful interests and winning. Miracle is running for the Supreme Court of Georgia to ensure that the State's highest court remains a place where the courtroom remains open and accessible to everyday citizens, and where the Constitution protects the people, not just the powerful. [] Jen Jordan, Georgia State Supreme Court (General Election (May), Flip) — Jen Jordan has spent 25 years as an attorney and then as a state senator fighting for everyday Georgians. Raised in Dodge County by a single mother who worked as a hairdresser, she learned the value of hard work and perseverance early. Throughout her career, Jen has worked to protect voting and privacy rights, hold corporate polluters accountable, and defend children from abuse. Jen is running because she knows that Georgians need a Supreme Court that will stand up and protect everyone's rights. [] Ruwa Romman, Georgia SD-07 (Primary Election) — State Representative Ruwa Romman is the first Palestinian elected to any public office in the state of Georgia. While some know Representative Romman as the Palestinian speaker who wasn't allowed onstage at the 2024 DNC, she has also been organizing in Georgia for over 12 years to flip the state. Ruwa is now running for State Senate because the old playbook has failed too many times. At a moment of fear and uncertainty, Ruwa believes that when we all organize, we can build a better future. [] Brenda Zamora, Nevada Clark County School District Board of Trustees District D (General Election, Protect) — Brenda Zamora is an immigrant daughter and mother of three who knows firsthand the challenges families face in education. Brenda's involvement in education advocacy began when her eldest daughter faced challenges early on, becoming her catalyst for community engagement. With four years on the Clark County school board, she has worked tirelessly to bridge the gap between families and schools, ensuring every voice is heard. She is deeply committed to protecting all our marginalized communities and making sure all families have a meaningful seat at the table. [] Winn Decker, North Carolina HD-37 (General Election, Flip) — Winn Decker is a Democrat running to flip North Carolina House District 37 in southern Wake County, one of the most competitive seats in the state. The son of two public school teachers from rural Tennessee, Winn came to North Carolina over a decade ago to earn his Ph.D. in Public Administration from NC State and put down roots in Fuquay-Varina. At the Hunt Institute, founded by former four-term Governor Jim Hunt, he worked across party lines with governors and legislators to strengthen public schools, expand access to higher education, and build a workforce ready for a changing economy. He coaches youth basketball and volunteers in the community he is fighting to represent. Winn's campaign is built around the pressures southern Wake families face every day: rising housing costs, unaffordable childcare, overcrowded schools, and a cost of living that keeps outpacing wages. He believes government can work for the people and is ready to prove it. So what does this mean? We're all in. | Peter,

Today, I voted against the County budget. And I did not make that decision lightly.

This budget includes important investments, including more funding for our schools and support for our public employees, public safety professionals, and nonprofit service providers. Those priorities matter deeply to me.

But I could not support a budget that still includes tax increases while families across Montgomery County are already struggling with the cost of living. [**_And we have our primary in almost a month, so if you agree that we can’t force our families to struggle even more, I hope you will stand with me by chipping in to my campaign_.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/131489132/621270701/-1721553747?refcode=BLU_EM_AFMC_2026-05-15_1&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjYjBhZjBkNy1iNDUwLWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ROtFaF6Lg76X18k6_xpcHpTt5dg50vgKm2sBmVeU-o0=)

Summit Ends With No Deals

President Trump [left Beijing](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL-OriAUxJ8GOwwewD8FxW3svtve0hwBlXwIBo_X3bffuMU-wFaTzCSTmd-_1_TCEENa_-LuTaFlctlN9poxJ9r8XEJ623wVWsK6UZ5AQMuF5o2eUpyayhlnHTa28qbpur7vO9lBtRmtB9trJdvBgRNKNb0D4eTQy1kqP9gqmKdK6EaDBFBDvahFQ2udluIRZEpg9IXq4o9rjsFiIjzfSy7W1zbvVTQb0XEy-YfByGC877su_iJfzid_nFyiYzDaLSRkMFK59oN_BH564qe3OTnu8JMTxvfJcSFfOGG4MfEbSwpp5T9_FYOxKsYdd4gxnG3HlFh3DPF7C_0C3X8DXwEAAP__x_R9mw) Friday with no major breakthroughs on trade, Taiwan, or Iran after a two-day summit with Xi Jinping. Xi secured legitimacy from the pageantry; Trump departed with warm words and photo ops but no binding agreements. Xi issued a stark warning in closed-door sessions that the U.S. and China "will have clashes" if [Taiwan's status](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0DFu7CAYBODT4G4t-A2GLShe425fmxLBD6zJsmBhHCu3j5wjpJqRRvqK-XiYh005led_-w669Wh89QYPZ2vpa3AtlRfWo_WYnmuvBijMNypuTJiSDRu89ugtwyFoJqVSSk4ShlWHmUsZUHKQgk8qRgl2dgLEJBkLXA1JXxQVTMAEwO9j5FHAjF5M9ApLOLU5tD62sB0uJ7Sl2_0Va8MwYn0PWa-9bzuZ_hFYCCzneY7O4bURWEo4dwKLbT1hDlfF_L19UsbUPdehab-dKee0z5Jw-nzblH_V_ocTvjT8BAAA___wYWq8) is mishandled -- underscoring that Beijing's core demands remain non-negotiable despite the cordial setting. [Trade talks](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLuOpDAURL_GZG4Zg3kEDjYh6003RBc_4HYbG5nrZTRfP6I_YaIjlY5Kpfr3nJ-AAeP6F3anM_nZJjubskCKtLklY3ybVDJ5XDdKsxSy40LxWs0xzHVltTUWalM5Xff9MAx908tq02psnHVu9KK1gwPhQXaj64UwyzKA8BXqu0qoWslGynZ8-NYr2RmrGnEDWCsguEyP7I6yBDQQCc63T9m4h0l7FfRGdJys-cPkxOR0XfbOmZzOVLLBuPJXKjlCYHKiDNZ9WPaDfyE3G0bgZ9l3JL44fN3-x-IEGb0_-UkZkHjyfEt5L9-cAC-IvJbNMKqubWompypre1wYAp5dz1qx7oDhs49-ced_LX8CAAD__ywzhw4) yielded nothing concrete. A framework the two leaders struck last October expires in November 2026, and no extension was announced. The meetings also produced no progress on Iran or rare earths. ★★★
Ratcliffe Lands in Havana

CIA Director John Ratcliffe [visited Havana](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckMHOpCAQhJ8GbxpoQZwDh714m73u0TANjp1BMdCO2bffuI_wn6qSSupL1Z_n_PSUaH__9lt0hZc55DDj-fJ55zW-Cu0fzGfhhd4r5xkkDK00rTLznmbVBBcweIVNdMracRxtb6FZnfS9kdJqQK2tUeoRwA5BDjjACIvFhtxdJY0y0APoR7foxcCAwfTyFi-09CkW7ko8zlci9Dv7-llywdhh3prkVuajiv6XgEnAdF1Xt_9l2mK9cwHTTRAwSSNgUlrAdFYB05ETMeFtkXwbqETkXNovVeLa3tu7lbfUFBeOi1KiOlih5XvzlP6T-QdHfR38CwAA___uI3Yq) Thursday, becoming the highest-ranking Trump administration official to travel to Cuba. His arrival came a day after Cuban officials announced the island had run out of fuel oil and diesel entirely. Cuba's [energy crisis](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LFu8yAUBeCnwVssfLHBGRj-xVv-tSO6XCCmIWBhErdvX7mP0Okc6UjfcD5u5oYxxXz_j0-vawvGFWfoZbHktnpbY35QedUW4n1txQAHeeHTZZhMTmbonHbkcKDO60GpeZ6VUNCtmqywOEvrAjgxgpwpXMXshRys5yhlF_VJ8WmYQACM1z6MYQJJbhL8DGQjx-Rr66vfXjZFwtxwf4RSyfdUnl3Sa2vbzsQ_BguD5TiO3lo6NwZL9sfOYMHaIiV_VnJq-66f_P2lSle1246YUtylYiO_PzGmX7X94YS3hp8AAAD__w1EbFE) has spiraled into a full collapse, with blackouts stretching across the island and the government acknowledging no reserves remain. The U.S. renewed an offer of $100 million in aid tied to political changes. Ratcliffe met with [Cuban intelligence](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckD1uxCAUhE-DO1vwAOMtKNK427Qp0TM_66dlzQrjOMePnCOkmmKkbzTf193dkTJtj098RVtbcqEE548Fy9bWuFTanr4ctSV6rK044DD2XPdCuy070QUbfEDhu2iFMdM0GWmgW60UU-AJVUSpFpgkmpvGCF4b5LfFjx3ZC8W10CAB1G1IKmkYfdCSX4FMccyxtqHG97Fk8rg13J-pVB8HX15dtmtr753JDwYzg_k8zwF_qOxXy2C--AxmrhnMQjGYPWFfsflMKcX--tg3zM-9r3hkaqWrNrxPypn20TDFHy-k_DfV_mHm28JvAAAA__811XH2) officials and senior government figures in a rare high-level diplomatic contact. No agreements were announced, and it remains unclear whether the visit signals a shift in the administration's Cuba policy. ★★★
Judge Balks on Mail Votes

U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols signaled reluctance Thursday to [quickly block](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2SrCAUhJ8GM6bgKP4EBDchm5tuaCEgsnMEC48zr7_lPsJGHXTXV13f13N-2oQpx_92D7rSOvviZ3cttmTawlJTfrlyVVpT3KjMIKDnQnGp5oyzbLz2zlvpmqDlMIzjOLQDNJtul05aF_peqNbDKNvJj4uEBSY_SaFck_SNEkoqaAG66bF2q4LeedWKOyzrhMVQ6VHDcS2YnM1kz9daqgsPV_YG9UZ0nKz9x8AwMLUgOot4lwzMjWdghGJgZMfAfF8-Bv4JKW4nd5tFDDmGk1PhVK_94KX6UHnJfLcJ-btQypFj2hOdDExTtT8-CTGd_cA6Ee_V7xH6g7e3hp8AAAD__9WSfHQ) Trump's executive order restricting mail-in voting, casting doubt on Democrats' bid for a fast preliminary injunction. The two-and-a-half-hour hearing raised skepticism about the timing. [Democratic lawyers](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2unTAQhJ_GdEb28mMoKNLQ3bQpkVmvD9Y1NrKXQ_L20ckjpJpmNKPv-_W1fdkQQ3r9tCcthf3mstvw3m1OfNBeQvrGfBf24XVw3kDBKNUg9bCluOnGLQ6d1djQoo2Zpsl0Bppj8XYmR2b2OMw0TQSTRrJKd0iwj2pswvKZUoMeoAPo59b3foAR3dCpT1jRKxupcFvouvcY0Ca29dvngtRiPpu4HMxXFd0PAauA9Xme9rH1COnFOV258qcmYL1yDBywClg_nwJWNQhYdS9g5XKfl6RIyCEnSb8Jbw5vkrk4KtLRmbFYrvKdmYqMobKA1e7O4Tyh7D0ZqbXXcjZkJACOCLP3yk1b5Vz-tAefsSmLu54QY6ijEb16nTbEfwz8H8rfC_wNAAD__4zTkXI) and civil rights groups argued Trump exceeded his authority by restricting mail voting and creating a national voter list, calling the order unconstitutional and likely to disenfranchise millions of eligible voters. The order [faces multiple suits](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2ypCAUhJ8GMyxEGJyAYBOz2XRDi58jsoNg4UH38bfmBvcBbtRBV3X19_15LS8TU8zht9lBV1wXX_zimjUl4wa2xvx2pVVcY9iwLJzxB2WSDnLJaRk6r73zZnAd6EGpaZrUqHi36SdMjEmlrAU_CiVWZsAKNwm5-icY6KL-TDE5SD5yLp79KlbJH87LkX3CEMFMgop9haPZFJ3JaM73WqqD3pW9S3pDPE4y_iJ8Jny-77uv0BDq-ekJnxMEkwifQ7mg5h0yEj7_bT4AvSGGjXrYi6sGT2qjpzYV96ZY236cFP6BaxgvoKV6qPQqGHOg3_yC8Lmr2h93TCmeD0UEC7uJ6esb_kDlpfn_AAAA___pp4WM) across federal courts, but the swift injunction Democrats sought appears increasingly unlikely based on Thursday's hearing. Courts may still rule against the order -- but not on the timeline challengers wanted.
